holds_back: The Money sheet lists the six most recent monthly cash rows; six is a display window, not a measured span.
replacement: A TUNABLE display window in the parameter table, checked against how many months a player scrolls back, or a chart that draws every kept row.

holds_back: Where last month went is grouped by the contract kind on each standing bill’s latest receipt plus the everyday living plan, standing in for the transfer’s reasonKey; a one-off transfer (a purchase, a fee, a gift) is not listed.
replacement: The accounts engine keeping each household transfer’s reasonKey on its journal receipt, so the sheet groups every outflow of the month by it.

holds_back: Someone close who runs a campaign is on its staff, cast as its team in scenes and the one who comes to canvass on election morning, but the campaign runs the same with or without them: the calls, the money and the volunteers' hours do not change.
replacement: Research what a local campaign's manager changes (follow-up calls, the volunteers' hours organized, the calendar kept) and have the campaign engine read staffIds where it decides those.

holds_back: Only full people who know a candidate offer to help once word of the filing reaches them; the counted population never offers, so a candidate's volunteers from the wider town come only from the campaign's own asks.
replacement: Counted groups who hear of a filing offer by the same volunteerReason times their count, filled in as full people when one offers to the player.

holds_back: A volunteer's evening of doors for a campaign the player's circle is in is kept as a volunteer-shift event (the volunteer, the candidate, whether it was their first evening, the hours, the doors knocked, the full people met and the counted residents reached), on their first evening and then at most once a week (volunteerShiftEventDays), that no scene, journal line or screen reads yet; the player sees their volunteers' work only in the voters it moved and the campaign's door count.
replacement: A director situation type (Words session) reading volunteer-shift events by id: a volunteer reporting back on their evening of doors, or the week's journal line of what the campaign's volunteers walked, with the volunteer-door causes that name the volunteer as actor.

holds_back: A cause group spends its money only on ad time, bought through the campaigns engine's ad purchase; it holds no events, sends no mailers and pays none of a cause's own costs.
replacement: A group chooses among the reach it can buy (events, mailers, press) and a cause's costs (a lawyer, a petition drive where the golden path needs one), read from its members' plans.

holds_back: candidacy.ts (incumbent tie) and legislature.ts (two member ties) still read a relationship's stored level, the closeness at the last contact, instead of today's faded closeness (closenessBetween).
replacement: Those three reads call closenessBetween(api.state, a, b) from src/core2/closeness.ts; then this row resolves.

holds_back: A known counted relative can receive a death notice, but opening full-to-counted family ties lack recorded closeness; grief is supported only where a relationship record already exists. No closeness is invented by the notifier.
replacement: Resolved Oct 23: the core opening records each full person's tie to a counted relative with openingClosenessHours (state.ts), the bench builds its relatives as counted records through the same opening, births-counted.test.ts fails on a tie without closeness, and births-counted-death-notice.test.ts follows a counted relative's death in a played year to the notice and the full relative's grief.

holds_back: The wider population's deaths and births come from rates applied to the counts each month: SSA cohort life tables scaled by the state's 2017 age-adjusted death rate against the nation's (NCHS), and NCHS 2024 national birth rates by mother's age. Whoever has the highest rate is the one who dies or gives birth; nobody's health or family plans decide it.
replacement: Deleted Oct 17 (claude/counted-drift-delete): the counted births and deaths are the renewal engine's counted flows (src/core2/births-counted.ts: NCHS state birth rates by mother's age, life-table chances with the state's death-rate ratio, deaths following serious illnesses), registered under SG-PW8-counted-arrivals; the old drift module ran only in life cores without the renewal engine and stood down in every played world.

holds_back: A counted worker whose job a public supplier agreement names as its qualified worker never dies or moves away in the counts.
replacement: When a named worker leaves, the agreement names another qualified worker at the supplier or ends (the finance engine's public supplier rules). Done Oct 14 (OPUS-CORE): supplier agreements now follow whoever does the work and end when nobody does (5ea270be on main), so named counted workers die and move like anyone else.

holds_back: Counted adults who give to a cause group give the mean of what the group's full members' own gift rule gives, once a month, because a counted giver has no drive or cash of their own.
replacement: Counted groups carry their own concern by topic and their cash above the buffer, so the same gift rule reads them directly, at the frequency full givers give.

holds_back: Newcomers to the wider population arrive only into homes a counted household just left, as a household of the same ages and genders with the home's cash, given names people born their year were called (SSA) and a family name drawn from the town's recorded names, and no retirement income or job (the jobs engine may hire them). The town's own state rates apply to every counted household, including relatives' households elsewhere. Leavers' cash stays in town.
replacement: Deleted Oct 17 (claude/counted-drift-delete): counted people move between places from causes in the counted-moves engine (src/core2/modules/counted-moves.ts), and newcomers are generated by the renewal engine's counted flows (SG-PW8-counted-arrivals); the drift module's own newcomer rule is gone.

holds_back: Engines that still read counted people one by one (jobs, business, campaigns, retirement claims, housing, place prices, candidacy) get a person or household record built on demand from the counted group's packed columns, with no past, no ties outside the household and no sources of their own.
replacement: Each engine reads counted groups and their counts (reachOf, group fields) instead of one counted person at a time; the views are then deleted.

holds_back: Money an engine pays to or takes from a place's counted residents as a whole (an owner's draw to owners who are counted, a pooled property tax bill, a price change on counted households, money left in the place's residents account) is shared by the place's counted groups by their people, not by the households it belongs to.
replacement: Each engine pays counted money through countedPayment with the counted person or household it belongs to (business owners, property tax by owner household, price changes by household), so the right group pays or is paid.

holds_back: Arrests follow the crimes this engine records and the police were told of (public safety reads its month record), at each offense's FBI clearance rate and the police the town's lines fund, as counted cases the justice engine files; no officer decides an arrest, so a reported crime is cleared as a share of the month, not one by one.
replacement: Police behavior that clears reported crimes one by one from the records (an officer, a lead, the victim's report), with the FBI clearance rates as the check on their totals.

holds_back: Which household is victimized is ranked by income, tenure and household kind (burglary) and by each member's age and income (violent crime), each read from a separate BJS table and multiplied as if independent. Property crime other than burglary uses the burglary ranking because BJS publishes no income or tenure cut for it in the tables used. The ranking overstates the gap between poor renters and rich owners; the place's expected count does not depend on it.
replacement: A joint rate by income, tenure and household kind from the NCVS public-use file or the NCVS Victimization Analysis Tool, and a property-crime cut of its own for theft and motor vehicle theft.

holds_back: A firearm homicide is a death, so the victimization records do not make it: crime.firearm-homicide (stand-your-ground-to-homicide, concealed-carry-permit-to-firearm-homicide) stays in the web's ledger and no death follows from it.
replacement: The death engine reading the web's factor for firearm homicide on each person's cause-specific mortality.

holds_back: Crimes happen to households with no offender: nobody decides to offend, so a victimization has no perpetrator, motive or relationship to the victim.
replacement: An offending engine where people decide to offend from their own traits, money and circumstances, so the national rate is a check on its total.

holds_back: Vandalism is not a victimization record: the NCVS has no national vandalism rate, so no household is victimized by it, and the web's crime.vandalism index (unemployment-to-vandalism, crime-level-to-vandalism) moves in the ledger only.
replacement: A sourced national rate for vandalism or criminal mischief (the NCVS household supplement or NIBRS destruction of property), then a record type like the others.

holds_back: Disasters happen only where and when FEMA declared one for the town's county or state (since 2000), as a public news event on the incident's start date. Federal Public Assistance obligated to the county's own government and the town's government (disasters declared since 2020) is paid in full on the declaration date from the U.S. Treasury outside account the game already keeps for Social Security. FEMA housing assistance approved for the town's households (Individuals and Households Program, owners and renters, disasters since 2020) is paid to the town's counted residents on the declaration date, scaled by the world's people over the Census estimate (a town without an estimate takes the whole amount); no single household is chosen, and 36% of household rows don't match a county or town by name. A government kept outside the world receives nothing. The town's households also pay, on the declaration date, for repairing the damage FEMA inspected in owners' homes (scaled the same way), to the town's open builders by their staff or to builders outside the town; the news event carries how many homes FEMA found damaged. Damage to rented homes falls on no landlord, and repairs are paid at once from what households have rather than over months or by insurance. No damage to businesses, public buildings or people; no other applicants (schools, utilities, nonprofits; 13% of assistance rows don't match a county); no new disasters after the records end.
replacement: The owner's ruling on what causes a disaster in play; damage to businesses, public buildings and people (from NOAA storm episodes), and household aid and repairs reaching the named households that lost homes, with insurance and repairs over time; assistance paid over its real obligation dates to every applicant; a federal FEMA account of its own.

holds_back: A town split between state legislative districts places its counted households into the districts by income order, filling each district in proportion to its Census population in the town, so each district holds a slice of the town's income ladder.
replacement: Each district's own Census tables (ACS by state legislative district: income, tenure, age) and its election results, so households are placed by the district's real mix.

holds_back: A full person's estate is their cash, the standing payments they owed, and the home of a household whose last member they were (sold when probate closes). Loans, businesses and accounts other than their main one are not settled. A relative who is still only a counted record does not inherit.
replacement: Probate that settles debts first, passes businesses by title, and reads a will where the person made one.

holds_back: An estate pays no estate or inheritance tax: no tax series exists for it in the law catalog yet.
replacement: Probate reads the estate and inheritance tax series in force for the decedent's state and the nation, pays the named treasuries, and the heirs take the rest.

holds_back: A person filled in from the wider population keeps receiving their retirement income through the residents account; their cash share is their opening share of the residents' current cash, and their job's calendar copies the employer's cadence from the fill-in date.
replacement: Done Oct 12: a filled-in retiree is paid their own award by the same outside payer on the same dates (the pooled retirement flow shrinks by exactly that amount). The cash share is an estimate from opening shares, and the job's calendar follows the employer's cadence, both by design.

holds_back: A filled-in household keeps its share of the place's unplaced workers' pay (counted workers no employer's books hold) as its own flow, untaxed, until it returns to the counts.
replacement: Resolved: a filled-in worker with an unplaced income holds a job (job:commuter:<personId>:<start>) at the place's outside account, paid through the payroll calendar with withholding; demotion ends it and returns the pay to the unplaced pool. Shown in unplaced-fill-in-job.test.ts (pool item core-commuter-job-fill-in).

holds_back: A named person filled in from a recorded identity (e.g. a state or federal official) gets neutral traits, no family or acquaintances, no cash and a monthly cadence.
replacement: PEOPLE's trait, kin and past builders seeded from the world seed and the identity (as fill-in of counted residents does), and the official's pay from the public payroll. Done Oct 12 (OPUS-CORE): fillInIdentity gives traits from PEOPLE's openingTemperaments, seeded by the world and the person.

holds_back: The federal government and other states pay their officials, and receive heirless estates, as outside governments, since only the town's own governments keep treasuries and the town's federal treasury holds only the town's own taxes. Offices the salary table lacks (an auditor, a public service commissioner) are paid the state treasurer's salary; the salary figures are recalled published values marked as estimates in the research file.
replacement: A salaried pay basis in the payroll engine so officials are paid by paycheck with withholding; every state's treasury where its officials act; sourced salary rows for every elected office.

holds_back: The federal government pays its officials (the president, vice president, senators and representatives), and another state's government pays its own, as an outside party recorded on the journal, and receives what escheats to it; their pay is paid in full while the taxes withheld from it go to every treasury the world keeps.
replacement: A federal treasury at national scale and a coarse treasury for every other state, so their officials are paid from them and their estates settle to them.

holds_back: The part of each household's assigned living cost (CEX basket plus HUD Fair Market Rent) that is not bought from a recorded local seller and is not carried by a bound contract (rent to a landlord, mortgage to the bank, which the housing engine pays) is paid to one outside account on the 1st: no utility or outside store.
replacement: The outside-spending model (category location-quotient leakage) that pays the non-local basket to outside sellers by category. Rent and mortgages are already paid to recorded landlords and the bank by OPUS-WORLD's housing engine (checked Oct 16, Rush Valley, Utah, seed rent1); turn the rest off with collapseToTwoLevels(input, { outsideLivingCosts: false }) once the model exists.

holds_back: Buyers outside the town are one account per place paying each firm a fixed weekly share of its projected receipts (adjusted with its demand), not individual outside customers, freight orders, Medicaid claims or guests.
replacement: Outside demand from the national and regional economy engines (OPUS-WORLD): exports, government programs and visitors as their own dated buyers.

holds_back: A full person out of the player's life for 180 days returns to their counted group (TUNABLE).
replacement: The owner's number of days. Owner ruling, Oct 15, 2026: 'The days without contact before a met person drifts back into the counted population is a per-world range of 180 to 240 days, drawn once per world at generation (seeded generation is allowed), never a single fixed number.' Built in counted-demotion.ts (demotionDays) from the countedDemotionDays spread.

holds_back: A counted person built at fill-in has their household, job and coworkers but no relatives living outside their household.
replacement: The owner's ruling; if wanted, the opening's relative generator run for one filled-in household, seeded by the world. Built: fillInPerson (src/core2/state.ts) rebuilds the filled-in household's past with buildDeepPast (family histories, src/core2/past-family.ts) and ties to relatives living elsewhere become husks (core.husks), met and filled in later; the opening keeps outside relatives as light husk-tier records (src/core2/data/opening-kin.json). The world-has-a-past work merged Oct 11 to 14.

holds_back: No appointer ever names the player to a town post; the player holds a post only by appointing others as the executive or by winning a seat.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either the player is never appointed, or an appointer's choice of the player becomes an offer the player accepts or declines in the conversation, and only an accepted offer fills the post. docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md, 'The player's choices are the player's' (Oct 14, night): 'No engine accepts a job, a home, a filing or any choice for the controlled person; the engine offers, the player decides.' Appointers never fill a post with the player on their own; an offer is the player's to accept.

holds_back: A town's districts are the state House districts its population splits into (from the place-district join), else the whole town; city council wards are not modeled.
replacement: The owner's ruling on what a town's districts are; wards as districts if he wants them. Answered by the owner's Oct 15 ruling and built in gov-council-election-method: each place's council is elected the way its own records say (councilElectionMethod in src/core2/gov-rules/council-election-method.ts: ward seats from a compiled charter, else estimated at large from the ICMA 2018 national shares, basis and citation kept on the office), and offices-local.ts seats the ward seats by part of town. The residents engine's split of a town into state House districts is a different thing (placement of counted voters for state legislative contests, SG-CORE-district-placement) and is not a council shape.

holds_back: A town larger than the opening target (10,000 people, owner decision Oct 9) opens with 10,000 people, not its Census population, so its counts, a law's reach and its money cover only those 10,000. A town smaller than the target opens at its real Census size.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either keep the cap, or let each counted group of a bigger town carry its Census count with the money and reach scaled to it. docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md, 'Town size (day-one audit)': 'a town opens at its real Census size; nothing pads it to 10,000. Follows one model, two tiers (counts must match the place).' Open for the engineers: population.ts still caps a town above the target; it follows the ruling next.

holds_back: Nobody holds anything in a trust: every estate passes through probate.
replacement: The owner's ruling on trusts: at least a revocable living trust a person can make, whose assets pass to its named beneficiaries at death without probate.

holds_back: Each firm pays cash above twice its industry's median buffer to owners monthly, a fixed tunable share to the town's residents and the rest outside; no firm has recorded owners, retained-earnings policy, taxes or investment.
replacement: OPUS-WORLD's business engine: recorded owners (local people or outside), payout and investment decisions from the firm's own conditions, and business taxes. Deleted the core stand-in (the monthly payout flow, its handler and its two parameters). Owners draw from their firm through the business engine: a recorded owner chooses a share of the profit the firm kept from their own money and the firm's cash (business.ts, owner-draw), to local owners as counted or full residents and to outside owners through the recorded outside exchanges.

holds_back: Archive stories use kinds prefixed 'archive:' in the news engine's story shape, and keep their facts on the story with a pointer in the reader's knowledge.
replacement: The press engine's own archive kind, written through its writer, once it lands.

holds_back: A counted resident's parent who died in the year before day one is not reported in the news archive.
replacement: The counted residents' parents' deaths archived at counted level.

holds_back: The prior election's challenger, a law's sponsor or signer who left office before day one, and the predecessors who held a seat are names drawn from the seed, not people of the world.
replacement: The core's fill-in makes a challenger or former official a full person the moment the player meets or looks them up, matching the name, party and record already written (OPUS-CORE fill-in).

holds_back: The news archive carries elections, laws, votes, budgets and the deaths of residents' parents, but no business closures from the year before day one. A counted resident's parent who died is not reported either.
replacement: Closures of the town's businesses in the year before day one, generated as records by the business engine, and the counted residents' parents' deaths archived at counted level.

holds_back: A territory's prior elections (its delegate and governor) count only the town's own ballots, since territories cast no presidential vote to scale from.
replacement: Each territory's certified 2024 delegate and governor returns (territorial election offices) as research data, read in place of the town's ballots.

holds_back: A law the research records only as in force at the opening (a state's policy answers, a law carried back to the start date) is given an enactment date between one and twenty years before day one, fixed by the world's seed.
replacement: Enactment years from the research for each policy answer, read by the law history (src/core2/past-laws.ts) in place of the seeded age; builder item core-past-law-enactment-years. Started Oct 23, 2026 in data/research/core/state-law-adoption-dates-2025.json for two policies, Medicaid expansion and right-to-work, all 56 places (Wikipedia summaries of the KFF tracker and the National Right to Work Committee timeline, whose own pages refused or showed the dates as images): their 67 laws in force at day one were passed 1.14 to 81.05 years before it, median 11.05. pastUndatedLawAgeYearsLow and High stay ESTIMATED (1 and 20) with those spreads (checked by scripts/research/core-parameters-check.ts).

holds_back: The town's families with school-age children are ranked by cash per child and the best-off enroll all their children in the private school until the town's state's private share of students (NCES, fall 2021) is reached, each paying the average private tuition. The family's beliefs, the schools nearby and the child's own needs do not yet enter, and enrollment is fixed at the opening.
replacement: PEOPLE's schools engine: each child's enrollment chosen from the family's income, beliefs and the schools nearby, moving as they change. Means-ranked enrollment replaced the even spread of the town's average on Oct 19.

holds_back: Each August the town's full families are re-ranked by cash per child and their private school tuition contracts start or end to match the NCES share; the counted families keep the enrollment they opened with.
replacement: Resolved: counted families are ranked with the full families each August (private-tuition-reenroll.ts) and their tuition is a part of the school's merged purchase flow, started or ended with setCountedTuition (modules/residents.ts). Shown in private-tuition-counted.test.ts (pool item core-private-tuition-counted).

holds_back: A town whose opening has no recorded teacher job to copy (no private school) gets no public school district.
replacement: The opening's jobs builder makes teacher jobs from the occupation's OEWS pay and a school-day timetable without a template.

holds_back: The wider population's purchases are merged per seller, kind and week of the month and paid monthly instead of after each household's own paydays; count workers always work their full schedule and are paid on the employer's cadence (semimonthly approximated as two monthly dates).
replacement: Wider-population spending timed from the counts' pay dates and income, and absence and turnover by industry read from the counts. The rows to check against are sourced (data/research/people/jolts-cps-turnover-absence-2025.json: BLS JOLTS 2025 annual hires, separations, quits and layoffs rates and CPS 2025 absence rates by industry), read by src/core2/turnover-check.ts; the mechanic that uses them is pool item people-residents-cadence-mechanic. Measured Oct 21 (Salem, Utah, seed 07f42052624493fd): hires 2.18 a month against JOLTS 3.3, quits 2.11 against 2.0, layoffs 0.27 against 1.1, separations 2.68 against 3.3.

holds_back: People who reach their claim age during play, full or counted, start a Social Security award sized like the opening's (a participant-average amount scaled by modeled covered months), paid monthly by the place's outside payer: to the person, or into their place's residents income while they're counted (it follows them when they're filled in). No application, earnings test, spouse or survivor benefit.
replacement: GOV's Social Security program: claims read the law in force and awards follow each person's recorded earnings.

holds_back: Every school-age full person attends the town's public school district (or, in a world opened without it, their town's schools as a place) on the weekdays of one national school calendar (Sept. 1 to June 10, cut at the state's required instructional days where it sets them in days (Education Commission of the States, 2018), the federal holidays by their dates each year, and fixed winter and spring breaks), for the national average school day. Attending is their own choice through the chooser against a full compulsory pull, so in practice every child goes every day: no illness, truancy or family circumstance keeps one home. No grade, class, teacher, homework, private school or homeschooling.
replacement: PEOPLE's schools engine: each child's enrolled school (opening-schools), its district calendar and hours, classes with classmates and teachers, and attendance that state law and family circumstances shape.

holds_back: At the opening (before any law can change), Social Security's earliest claim age, full retirement age by birth year and the age-70 end of delayed credits are read from a core data table of the same statute GOV's law rows hold. During play, claims are dated from the law in force (GOV's socialSecurityAges) wherever the laws engine runs; a claim already dated keeps its date if Congress changes the ages later.
replacement: GOV's Social Security ages as law in force (lawInForce), read at the claim date. Done Oct 15 (claude/ss-ages-law-in-force): retirementClaimAgeMonths takes the ages from the law (socialSecurityAges, the law in force at the claim date, or the day-one law for the opening's history); the core table src/core2/data/social-security-ages.json is deleted.

holds_back: The villages of Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands come from the game's existing recorded list (carried over from the old place module), not from Census identities.
replacement: Census 2020 Island Areas place identities (the research request territory-place-identities), read into the same listing. Oct 14 (OPUS-CORE): the candidate list is built (src/core2/data/places/territory-places-census.json, 158 inhabited villages with Census GEOIDs and 2020 populations, every current key kept, by tooling/build-territory-places.ts); the swap waits until PEOPLE's population builder reads places through the core lookup.

holds_back: Counted residents the opening couldn't place in a town firm (the employment target from ACS/CPS less recorded jobs) earn the place's ACS median earnings (the town's median recorded wage where the place's sample is too thin), paid every two weeks from outside, without employers, commutes or industries.
replacement: Recorded jobs for every employed resident: town firms in the missing industries (health care, education, government) and commutes to employers in other places (LEHD LODES origin-destination flows), with their own pay.

holds_back: A business closed by its owner's choice pays its workers what they've earned (counted workers at once, full workers on their next payday from cash held back), its supplier bills already owed, then settles each open credit line from the cash left (the rest is written off, as in any closure); no assets are sold, so a firm's equipment and property add nothing to what lenders and the owner receive.
replacement: The closure sells the business's assets (WORLD's business engine records them) before settling lenders and the owner's distribution.

holds_back: Counted adults in the town vote as one group per age band: eligible voters are the count times the place's ACS 2020–2024 citizen share of adults blended with the state's CPS 2024 share for the band, turnout is the state's CPS 2024 citizen turnout (national rows where no state row exists, as for the island areas), and every group starts with its county's 2024 presidential two-party margin as its lean (the state's in Alaska, which reports by house district).
replacement: Residents' own views (PEOPLE's views engine) set each group's lean, refined by GOV's elections; each counted person's own citizenship once the counts record it.

holds_back: The job-offer scene composes only once the Words lead adds `job-offer` lines (scene-talk and scene-words banks) for the purpose; until then the director stages no call for a job-offered record, so the player sees no offer and it lapses at its deadline.
replacement: Resolved Oct 28 (words and director session): the scene-talk bank holds the job-offer purpose's lines (the call, the offer with the position and the hourly pay from the offer record, the four replies, the follow-ups and closes); purpose-scene words the offer record's employer, position, pay and deadline; the job-offered record joins scheduling.ownRecordScenes, so the call stops the day.

holds_back: How often a scene from circumstance may come (the days between two), how strongly it orders the journal, and how the cast is weighed (named, witnessed, the player's tie, sociability).
replacement: A calibration against the owner's playtests: scenes from circumstance per played month and how many he skips.

holds_back: The clerk who takes a filing is left unfilled in a scene: the filing visit shows the player and the office's title, with no clerk in the room.
replacement: A clerk's office has a clerk: a full person on the town's payroll or an elected holder, read by the clerk fill (pool item gov-clerk-person).

holds_back: The person who tells someone a law changed their check is the head of the outlet whose story taught them; no record names who told them in person, and a notice from the probate court has no teller at all.
replacement: The owner's ruling: either the person who retold the story (the speech engine's retelling record) or an outlet's reporter, read by the teller fill.

holds_back: Conversations omit introducing or asking after relatives shared by the speaker and listener instead of naming their shared relation naturally.
replacement: Resolved: a relative two people share is asked after as they call them, by the kin address in src/director/data/journal-rows.json (Dad, Mom, Grandma, Grandpa) or a shared sibling's first name, through the conversation bank's family lines (pool item words-family-talk-kin-address).

holds_back: What a heard speech was given at (a campaign stop, a meeting remark, a hearing), and how a candidate gave it (a town hall, a campaign speech, a debate), is read from the shape of the speech's record id, because the speech engine's record carries no occasion.
replacement: An occasion fact on every speech.heard record, and the campaign act on a candidate's, written by each producer (campaigns, meetings, legislature, parties, press, the governor's address), read here first.

holds_back: A state's fiscal laws (a balanced operating budget, funding pensions to schedule, a minimum reserve balance) move what it pays to borrow (the outcome web's gov.borrowing-cost, in basis points), and the treasury reprices the state's whole interest line by that change over the state's own rate on its debt at once, as if every bond it owes were issued at the new spread. County and city interest lines do not read it. The federal-deficit link runs (federalDeficitChangePct reads the federal budget row against its base) but only the state's interest line reads it. The newspaper-closure link into the same spread still does not run: it has its cause now (the closed local newspapers the press module records) but no size, because the study prices a county's own bonds after its county paper closes and no county or city interest line reads the spread.
replacement: A bond record per government (issue date, amount, coupon, maturity) from the Census debt outstanding, with new issues priced at the spread the web keeps, so a law's change reaches only the bonds issued after it, and local governments' spreads read the same measure.

holds_back: The loan-rate-cap links move the count of consumer lenders (payday, title and installment) per 100,000 residents.
replacement: Resolved Oct 29 (world-small-dollar-lenders): the credit engine's small-dollar lender is the high-cost lender product, and it reads the web's factor on finance.high-cost-loans through webReach where it quotes a loan (householdApplications in src/core2/modules/credit.ts), so the loan-rate-cap links change what it lends.

holds_back: A severe disaster raises a place's non-disaster public transfers.
replacement: Budget transfers split by disaster and non-disaster that the disaster link's factor multiplies.

holds_back: Student-debt relief and an abortion denial each move households' past-due debt.

holds_back: A state or federal officeholder outside the town is a stable identity (name, gender, birth date, party) with no core2 person behind it.
replacement: CORE's two-level fill-in builds the full person from this identity (seeded from the world and the seat), with kin and a past from PEOPLE.

holds_back: When the federal Social Security line is cut or raised, the retirement awards the opening wrote for full people keep their amount; only awards claimed during play follow the line.
replacement: setStandingContractAmount accepts a recipient-income contract's new benefit level from its next due date, and applySocialSecurityLevel sets it, with the funding contract that pays it.

holds_back: Donors outside the town (askOutsideDonors, for seats wider than the town) give only the savings share of the person rule (donationShareOfCashPerWarmth), and on a typical donor's whole account balance one for one (medianTransactionBalance at outsideDonorIncomeUsd), not as a named donor does on the savings beyond a cushion of their living costs, weighed on a log scale of that cushion; the share of a month's income after bills that a named donor also gives from (giftBudget, donationShareOfMonthPerWarmth, weighed on a log scale of donationMonthScaleMonths of their living costs) is not read for them.
replacement: Read a typical donor household's monthly living costs for the place group (the same living-cost tables the population is built from), make the cushion and the month's spare from them, and give by donationAnswer's two log-scaled shares, so outside and named donors use one rule; recheck the outside share of a campaign's receipts against localInPlaceDonorShare (0.65, 0.25 to 0.95).

holds_back: A national race's pool (the presidency) holds every member of Congress, the town's own state's legislators and every place's governor and statewide officers, but not another place's legislators (about 7,400 seats): they are named officials on their term rows (personId null, the CTO's ruling of Oct 29, 22:40), and the pool weighs only full people, so none of them weighs running for president. Before U1 an 8-member sample of each other chamber, full people, stood in for them.
replacement: Another place's legislators weighed from their term rows by the same reasons as a full official (the seat's reach, the party's backing, an ambition read from the seat), the way candidacy's counted screen weighs counted residents, and filled in only when one runs.

holds_back: Another place's statewide office elected without party labels (about ten: superintendents of public instruction in California, North Dakota, Washington and Wisconsin, Oregon's labor commissioner, Hawaii's Office of Hawaiian Affairs trustees, D.C.'s state board of education president, Guam's public auditor and utilities commission, the Northern Marianas board of education) is seated at the opening but never raced, so its holder serves past the end of the term on its row.
replacement: A nonpartisan count for a race the town doesn't vote in (the incumbent against a challenger drawn from the state, decided by the places' votes on the candidates' own standing), so the seat loop in racesIn races these offices like every other.

holds_back: An official of another state (not federal, not the player's own state) has no pay row, post, living cost or paycheck until the player knows them or they are in focus (the people keepsWhy keeps a why for); they are paid from the payday after, with no back pay, so their account starts at the savings a family at their pay keeps, not at what a year of paychecks would have left.
replacement: Name and seat the other states' officials only when something asks for them (pool item gov-outside-officials-built-on-demand), so an official met later comes with a past that matches the seat's pay and years served.

holds_back: Each month, a state, county, city or federal treasury receives from the town's outside account an even twelfth of the yearly revenue no flow in the game pays (state and federal aid come from the treasury above it; corporate, customs, excise, estate and gift, selective sales and vehicle taxes, and charges and fees, come from named groups of payers on their due dates), and pays each spending line an even twelfth: what the town's engines paid on the line stays in town, the town's share of purchases goes to its businesses, and the rest goes to the outside account as spending elsewhere.
replacement: Each revenue line from its real payer on its real dates, and each spending line to its real payees on theirs.

holds_back: Another place's holder whose party neither the legislative roster nor the research (data/research/offices/unrecorded-holder-parties-2026.json) reads sits with no party on the term: six vacant legislative seats with no Ballotpedia vacancy row (Florida, Massachusetts, Missouri, New York), Guam's attorney general and the Virgin Islands board of elections (eight seats). Filled in as a person (holderOf in src/core2/modules/officials.ts), such a holder keeps the term's no party, so the person matches the term row, never the 2024 state-lean estimate. A race for such a seat fields both major parties as if it were open.
replacement: Each seat's holder read into the research file (the chamber's own member page or the territory's election results), so seatOutsideOffices seats them in their party.

holds_back: Every state seat the world races outside the town (each other place's legislators, governor and statewide officers, and the town's own state's districts that do not cover it; thousands of seats in an even year) keeps, every cycle, its race row, its count's results and places, the ended term beside the new one and the took-office record, and nothing folds the old ones once play no longer reads them. In Long Hill, Connecticut (seed m7b, four played years to January 2029) the offices engine's terms grow from 21,136 rows to 33,973 (main at the branch's base: 644 to 1,044), and the voting engine's races, results and returns from 185 to 13,932 rows each and its places from 624 to 40,981; November 2026 alone races 6,923 seats (Leola, South Dakota, seed m2-nov1). The took-office records themselves are not kept in the town's log (they are placed in the office's own place).
replacement: A fold of each outside seat's ended terms, race rows and results older than its last few cycles into one summary row per seat (who held it, in which party, from and to), its readers' windows named, proven by a long save's records kept (pool item core-long-run-tables-grow-with-history).

holds_back: Another government's legislature session (a state the player is not in) is simulated once, when it convenes, from its members' opening views and its executive's: a change passes when every chamber has more members for it than against it and the executive agrees (or both chambers hold two thirds); it writes one law row with the chambers' counts on a day inside the session, and no filing, bill, committee, per-member vote or event. No settledness, reluctance, sponsor, deal, lobby or press term decides it, and a member's views do not move during the session.
replacement: Add the terms that matter to a played proof, each read at the chamber's level (how fresh the law is, the executive's reluctance to reverse it), through the same counted-group rule as a full member; and build members on demand rather than at the opening (core-fill-in-hook).

holds_back: Another place's statewide officer whom the law elects on one ticket with the governor (a lieutenant governor in about thirty places, data/research/offices/state-offices.json electedWithGovernorOnTicket) is raced on its own seat, the same as every other statewide officer, so the count can seat a lieutenant governor of a different party from the governor elected the same night.
replacement: A ticket office's race decided with its governor's: the governor race's winning party seats the running mate the same day, read from the office's research row.

holds_back: Where a place's filing row in data/research/elections/filing-requirements.json gives its signature rule as a formula (for example a share of the votes cast for the office at its last election: 27 municipal, 21 county, 14 state legislative, 13 statewide and 13 U.S. House party rows) or gives nothing, the filing's petition asks the median of the read counts for its office family and side (an independents' row that is not its own reads the party row): for a party filing 28 municipal, 50 county, 113 state legislative, 2,000 statewide and 500 U.S. House; for an independent 30, 25, 125, 3,501 and 1,000.
replacement: A structured threshold for each formula row, its base read from the world's own results through the recall engine's signatureBase (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts), the median kept only where a row gives nothing.

holds_back: A local race's petition asks at most petitionMaxShareOfVoters (10%) of the town's voters, at least one, wherever the law's count or the estimated median would ask more: one share for every place, not each place's own percentage, minimum and maximum.
replacement: Each place's own petition formula read into data (its percentage, base, minimum and maximum) and applied to the town's voters, so the cap is the law's own and no common share is needed.

holds_back: Where a contest's district reaches past the town (a county seat drawn as a state's places, a legislative, U.S. House or statewide race), the clerk counts the town's share of the law's signatures, by the town's eligible voters over the district's, at least one: the signatures a candidate would gather in the places the world holds only as counts are neither gathered nor checked.
replacement: Signatures gathered in the district's other places at a coarse step, from the campaign's effort there, checked against the law's whole count.

holds_back: Every campaign act that carries one question (a donor meeting, an event, an ad, a mailer, an evening of doors) carries the campaign's lead (platformLead), so everything a candidate chooses to say in a race is on one question, the top score of their platform; the other platform questions are heard only where the whole platform is (a door, an interview answer).
replacement: Each act's topic taken in turn over the platform, the question furthest behind its score's share of what the campaign has said so far (no roll), so a candidate's messages and speeches follow the score shares; C1 then measured from those records.

holds_back: A candidate's platform score leaves out the research rule's record factor, (1 + platformRecordWeight x record(q)): a question the candidate's own votes, job or past acts bear on favorably scores no higher than one they have no record on.
replacement: record(q), 0 to 1, read from the candidate's recorded votes on the question (StanceReader.votesOn, the votes a voter's record reader already reads) and their job's tie to it, weighted by a platformRecordWeight row (TUNABLE, 0.5, spread 0 to 1, Sellers 1998), with C1 kept in its band with it on.

holds_back: platformSupportSlope is the study's domestic coefficient carried over, and the played total it is checked against does not reach the research's band. The research's C1 (docs/research/platform-emphasis-2026-10-30.md, as its quote verification restates it: +16% to +86% emphasis per 10 points of support), measured from what candidates said by record (messages and speeches on each question they hold a view on, silences included, each candidate offset by how many questions they hold a view on) over 42 candidates in four drawn places' years (run seed b6c9d59eda6a31f1, src/core2/campaign-platform-played.test.ts), gives -3% at the slope's value 0.035; with each campaign's lead chosen again from the recorded scores, -16% at 0 (the old rule), -10% at 0.015 and -3% at 0.028, 0.043 and 0.062. No slope in the research's spread brings it in. Every act carries the campaign's lead alone (SG-GOV-platform-emphasis-lead-only), so each candidate's emphasis is all on their top score, the fit within one candidate's questions has no finite value, and the pooled total is set by the differences between candidates; over every slope from 0.028 up the top score does not change. Earlier measures on score shares (-13% pooled, +345% to +712% within candidates) overshoot or miss for the same reasons: picking the top 3 with silences sharpens the slope, as the research's C1 warns.
replacement: The slope measured into the C1 band once a campaign's acts share its emphasis over the platform by score (SG-GOV-platform-emphasis-lead-only's replacement), by the pooled total with each candidate's offset, and the played-year test holds the band again: pool item campaign-platform-emphasis-c1. Until then the test prints C1 and does not hold it (governing lead, Nov 2, under the CTO's Nov 1 ruling that an unmet calibration line is reported in the PR and carried to its own item, never tuned or widened to pass).

holds_back: A candidate choosing which questions to run on reads the true share of the town's electorate on their side of each question (electorateSides: every named adult at their own view, every counted record at its record's stance times the people it stands for, by the stance the ballot reads a voter's agreement from), as if they knew it exactly. For a ward, county, state or federal seat it is still the town's electorate, so a statewide candidate is scored against one town.
replacement: The candidate's belief about support, read from the people they know and the polls and news they have received, so it leans toward their own side and their circle (Pereira, APSR 2021: local officials misjudge majority opinion and overestimate support for the policies they endorse) and toward the conservative position, more for Republicans (Broockman and Skovron 2018: Republicans overestimate support for the conservative position on every issue by over ten points and often by over twenty, Democrats by less), with the seat's own electorate (its ward, county or state) in place of the town's.

holds_back: A governor the player plays never declares a state of emergency: the engine does not declare for them, and no office screen offers the declaration when a disaster is recorded in their state.
replacement: Resolved Nov 8 (Legislation): the disaster waits as an offer (`emergencyOffers`), the state day brings it to the governor as an `emergency` entry that holds the player, and the player declares through declareEmergency or lets it pass. Was: an office-screen stop the day a federally declared disaster is recorded in the player governor's state, offering declareEmergency with the hazard record and the state's power named, or leaving it to the character.

holds_back: A colleague the player owes a favor from a deal never asks the player to repay it: their campaign skips the player when it calls in favors, because the engine never answers for the player and no scene puts the ask to them.
replacement: The colleague's campaign writes a favor-asked record naming the obligation; the director stages the ask, and the player's answer endorses (settling the obligation) or refuses.

holds_back: Inherited game-profile powers cells are provisional estimates; a cell explicitly marked limited retains a disputed grant while its qualitative conditions are not yet all executable predicates. A territory's unread cell is its state cell (data/research/powers-catalog/territory-grant.json), an estimate.
replacement: Sourced per-place cells and structured conditions for each limited power, evaluated by the same authority reader before introduction or an executive order. Researched Oct 23, 2026 (research-core-sourced-parameters): NACo Research (2022) county authority by state (a level from 1, Dillon's Rule, to 6, home rule, with the home rule option and Dillon's Rule flexibilities) for all 56 places in data/research/core/naco-2022-county-authority.json, the per-place input for the county cells whose condition is home rule or Dillon's Rule. Still open: no limited cell's condition is an executable predicate yet; the builder item core-policy-authority-limited-cell-predicates reads the file in src/core2/policy-authority.ts. Territory cells stay with laws-territory-powers-research.

holds_back: A question with no mapping in the powers catalog, or a local question whose gating state law is not on record, cannot be introduced; the authority result records a disputed missing grant rather than silently permitting the action. (Oct 15: a territory's cell the catalog has not read now takes its state cell, an estimate; see SG-GOV-policy-power-conditions.)
replacement: The gating state laws recorded in the opening law table for every place, read before introduction and executive orders.

holds_back: Where the town's records hold no government building, its polling places have no building and a kind of "unread"; where they hold one, every precinct votes in it.
replacement: Each precinct votes in one of the town's own buildings of a fitting kind (schools, churches, halls, government buildings), sharing a building as the place's precincts do. Researched Oct 23, 2026 (research-elections-sourced-parameters): data/research/elections/eavs-2024-polling-places.json holds the EAC's 2024 EAVS (public release V2) precincts, election-day polling places and early-voting sites for all 56 places, and facility shares measured in one state (County Commissioners Association of Pennsylvania, May 2026: religious 31 percent, government 19, schools and libraries 15, public safety 14, community and club 12, commercial and other 9), ESTIMATED for the rest. The builder item elections-polling-places-by-building-kind reads it in src/core2/modules/voting.ts pollingPlaces().

holds_back: A presidential year's national environment is a fixed shift against the party holding the presidency, with no economy or presidential record behind it.
replacement: A national environment read from the economy (WORLD macro) and the president's record, replacing the fixed incumbent-party shift.

holds_back: Uses the CTO ruling that working press staff and outlet owners cannot run for office while retaining that role.
replacement: Owner confirmation or revision of the press-employment conflict rule; apply the chosen rule to all candidate filing paths. Done Oct 19 (gov-press-ban-withdrawn): the owner withdrew the ban on Oct 16 ("a reporter who wants to run may run"; OWNER-DECISIONS). The press-employment check is gone from checkEligibility, the candidacy chooser and the candidate pool, so press staff file and run like anyone; only the automatic vacancy stand-in still passes over press jobs, because the defect was a reporter seated without an election.

holds_back: A local outlet's record name is its kind (newspaper, television, radio); outlets are sized from state counts, not named real outlets.
replacement: Names from the English engine (OPUS-PEOPLE) and per-county outlet rosters from Medill and FCC data.

holds_back: A sourced survey ratio of all property taxes paid to home value stands in for researched individual statutory levies. The shared reader uses it only until an actual property-tax amount supplies the series; it cannot reconstruct the separate levies from that aggregate.
replacement: Source each applicable levy and its taxing body, assessment base and effective dates; combine actual levies through the existing resolver and tax engine.

holds_back: Every owner's property tax goes to the county treasury (the city's, else the state's, where there's no county government), which keeps every level's share.
replacement: The collector remits each level's share by its Census property-tax revenue line, on the county's own due dates.

holds_back: The opening's public employers in town (schools, police, fire, county offices) pay their workers from outside accounts; the treasury's lines for that work pay the outside account instead of those employers.
replacement: Each public employer draws its payroll from its government's treasury, and the close counts it as that line's in-town spending. Resolved by Claude Sonnet session, October 16, 2026: the budgets engine calls api.fundPublicPay for every opening public employer, linking it to its government's treasury (matched by government key); the employer's wages leave the treasury's account on the payday journal, the close counts them as that line's in-town spending, and what the treasury couldn't cover is a public-pay shortfall on the month's treasury row. What the lines still pay the outside account is spending outside the town's employers.

holds_back: The public pay floor's employer-to-level map is a first cut (public schools count as town employers). A public post filled by the government (an aide, a department head) is paid at the floor in force the day it is filled, and a jobs-engine opening at the floor in force the day it is posted. Councils, legislatures and Congress can now draft it from the bill catalog (OPUS-GOV, Oct 14).
replacement: School districts as their own level of government, and the hiring engines (OPUS-WORLD) reading the floor when they set a new public hire's pay.

holds_back: A recall bar that a statute counts in calendar months is stored in src/core2/data/campaigns/recall-bars.json as a fixed number of days: six months as 182 days (Louisiana's closing bar, Nebraska's and Nevada's opening bars, and the earlier Arizona and Oregon opening bars and California's closing bar) and two months as 61 days (Montana's opening bar). Six calendar months run 181 to 184 days and two run 59 to 62, depending on the date counted from, so the stored bar can admit a date the statute bars or bar one it admits by up to three days: for a term ending January 1, 2027, July 2, 2026 is inside six months but 183 days away, and Louisiana's 182-day bar admits it. Each of these rows is ESTIMATED with its spread.
replacement: Builder item gov-recall-bars-calendar-months: a bar row may state calendar months (opening and closing), and the recall engine compares the date with the term's start plus those months, or its end less them, so the rows are SOURCED from their statute quotes. Until then they are ESTIMATED in src/core2/data/campaigns/recall-bars.json and data/research/core/recall-timing-statutes-2026.json, and scripts/research/check-core-research.ts recomputes each spread from the calendar.

holds_back: One national bar on when a local recall may start (not in a term's first 180 days; not again in a term after one failed), not each state's own statute.
replacement: Each state's recall timing bars read into the municipal rule pack and resolved like its threshold and window. Oct 23, 2026 (research-core-sourced-parameters): twelve more places read from statute (AK, DC, FL, GA, LA, MT, NE, NV, ND, SD, WA, WY; 5 SOURCED and 7 ESTIMATED: ND and WA where the bar counts from an election, FL where the bar is a fraction of the term, SG-GOV-recall-bars-term-fraction, and LA, MT, NE and NV where the bar is counted in calendar months and stored as days, SG-GOV-recall-bars-calendar-months) into src/core2/data/campaigns/recall-bars.json, read by recallBarsFor in src/core2/modules/recalls.ts, with the quotes and each state's bar after a failed recall in data/research/core/recall-timing-statutes-2026.json (checked by scripts/research/check-core-research.ts); 21 of the 22 places with a petitioned local recall now have a bar read from their own statute, seven of the twelve new ones estimates. Still open: no Mississippi timing bar was read, so the national estimate stands there; bars counted from an election (NE, WA, ND) and each state's rule after a failed recall wait on the builder item gov-recall-bars-election-clock.

holds_back: A recall bar that a statute sets as a fraction of the term (Florida: one-fourth of the term, Fla. Stat. 100.361(8)) is stored as two day counts: one for terms of up to longTermAboveYears years and one for longer terms. recallBarsFor returns the same 365 days for a three-year term as for a four-year term, 91 days more than one-fourth of three years (273.75 days), and about 183 days fewer than one-fourth of a six-year term (547.5 days). The row is ESTIMATED with a spread of 182 to 365 days, the statute's bar for terms of 2, 3 and 4 years. Today every Florida council, mayor and county commission seat takes four years, where the value is exact.
replacement: Builder item gov-recall-bars-fraction-of-term: a bar row may state a fraction of the term, and recallBarsFor in src/core2/modules/recalls.ts turns it into days for the term at hand (term years x 365.25 x the fraction), so the row is SOURCED from the statute's own quote. Until then the row is ESTIMATED in src/core2/data/campaigns/recall-bars.json and data/research/core/recall-timing-statutes-2026.json, and scripts/research/check-core-research.ts checks that the statute's days for terms of 2, 3 and 4 years fall inside its spread.

holds_back: A counted voter weighing a recall over misconduct, or the member's answer to the petition at the due day's count, reads the share of the town's named adults who heard of it as their own exposure, since counted residents keep no record of the stories they heard.
replacement: A per-group hearing record for counted residents, kept by the news engine, that the recall reads like a named voter's.

holds_back: A recall petition's required signatures read the state's named base from the world's records where it holds them (votes cast for the office, or at the town's last election of that level, from the recorded results). Where it holds none, the base is sized from the real averages: registered voters (the town's eligible voters times the national registration share), the last gubernatorial vote (the town's population times the voting share, scaled to a midterm), and votes cast before the town has held an election.
replacement: Registered voters read from the town's rolls and the town's share of the last gubernatorial vote read from the state's returns, once the world keeps them.

holds_back: How soon a body may undo a law it passed: no place's data records a reconsideration rule, so a sliding reluctance (fresher law and wider margin, more reluctance; a member's own last vote) stands in for the rule.
replacement: The owner's ruling on reconsideration, and each place's recorded rule as data where one exists. Resolved 2026-10-14: Owner ruling (docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md): 'Repealing a fresh law: the body's own rules from data; where none, a sliding reluctance from how recently and by how much it passed. No fixed cooldown.' The reluctance is that rule (OPUS-GOV, Oct 14).

holds_back: A state's or county's rent-help line is paid to the played town by the town's share of the government's population, as though renter households were spread the same way as people.
replacement: Record renter households per government (counted, as the town's are) and pay each line by the town's share of them; the stopgap clears when the share reads renters.

holds_back: A world candidate's campaign day (rivalDay) never holds a donor meeting at a supporter's home; its money comes only from call time, the turn's asks and the outside donors. Because rivalDay never takes it, campaignDayChoices with world=true skips the host scoring entirely (src/core2/campaign-day.ts, same marker) and reports the donor-meeting choice unavailable with no host, so a rival's turn reads nobody's circle for it.
replacement: campaignDayChoices names a host for world candidates too (the world=true skip in campaign-day.ts is deleted), rivalDay scores the donor-meeting choice on the same scale as the event and the interview (rising as the bank empties and with the host's warmth), takes it as the day's whole act when it scores best, and the world's races are re-checked against the campaign-finance calibration.

holds_back: A government's charges and fees (tuition, hospital bills, sewer and trash, parks, tolls) are paid by the town's households in proportion to the living cost each pays on the 1st, split by what the charges are for from the Census 2022 item codes; no household chooses to use a service, no business pays a charge of its own, and a household that uses none still pays its share of the living cost.
replacement: Each service paid by the people who use it on the day they use it: tuition by enrolled students' households, hospital charges by patients' visits, sewer and trash by dwellings and businesses, parks and tolls by trips, from the school, health and travel engines. (pool item gov-service-charges-by-use).

holds_back: A special election for a seat no race engine counts (a statewide executive seat, a judge, a seat of another body) goes to the best-suited eligible person on the day instead of a vote. The town's own seats are real races in the voting engine, and a House or legislative district outside the town is counted by the world races (named party candidates, the winner serves the unexpired term). The date is the state's law for the office where special-election-law.json reads it, else the 90-day estimate (SG-GOV-special-election-timing).
replacement: Each office's special-election timing from its law (many fill at the next general election).

holds_back: The date of a special election where the state's law for that office family is not read: 90 days after the vacancy. Only California's U.S. House and legislative rows are read in special-election-law.json.
replacement: A row per state and office family in src/core2/data/elections/special-election-law.json read from the state's code.

holds_back: Officials' automatic hires (an aide at the monthly staff review, a department head refilled at the executive's review) choose only among people out of work, though anyone paid less than the post would apply.
replacement: Resolved Oct 19: taking a public post ends the job the person held (startPublicJob), so an aide, a department head and a state cabinet nominee may come from a private job when the post pays more than they earn; someone who has worked today leaves for a post tomorrow. Shown in staff-hire-employed.test.ts (pool item gov-stopgap-staff-missing-engine).

holds_back: A staffer hired where no government treasury is open (no budgets module) holds the post without pay; with budgets open they're on the payroll of the government their official serves.
replacement: Resolved Oct 20: a staffer whose office employer sits where no job exists to follow (a territory's state or federal office) takes the town's schedule and payday (scheduleFromPlaceId), so every aide hired where budgets are open is on a treasury payroll. Shown in staff-paid-every-place.test.ts (pool item gov-stopgap-staff-missing-engine).

holds_back: A law whose first recorded phase begins after the January 20, 2025 start (most income tax, sales tax, property tax, SNAP, unemployment and Medicaid rows begin October 2025 or January 2026) is in force from the start at that phase's terms, labeled as an estimate.
replacement: Oct 23, 2026 (research-law-reach-sourced-parameters): the phases in force on January 20, 2025 are now sourced and built for the federal income tax and Social Security wage base (IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40, Publication 15 2025), every state's income and sales tax and average local sales tax (Tax Foundation, January 1, 2025), SNAP maximums (USDA FNS FY2025), the Medicaid match for all 56 places (HHS FY2025, FR Doc. 2023-25636 and 2024-27938) and unemployment weekly bounds (DOL, January 2025), in data/research/laws/*-2025-*.json, written by scripts/research/build-starting-law.py and checked by scripts/research/check-start-law-2025.ts; rowsCarriedToStart in src/core2/modules/laws.ts no longer reaches those series. Still carried back (research-start-law-remaining-2025-phases): county and city income taxes, city sales taxes, county, city and some state minimum-wage tiers, state corporate income tax, local income tax authority, unemployment program terms, and the five territories' income and sales taxes.

holds_back: A contest filed with a state or territory election board, commission or division (not the secretary of state) names no clerk: the filing scene shows the office's title with no one at the counter.
replacement: Resolved Oct 16: the executive engine seats a chief election official for the state (appointment post chief-election-official), a full person on the state payroll, and the filing clerk returns them (pool item gov-state-election-office-holder).

holds_back: 60 of 261 statewide executive offices (superintendents, insurance, labor and land commissioners, commissions and boards, D.C. and the territories) take their holder's party from rows not verified against a live source (data/research/offices/statewide-executive-parties-2026.json); 201 rows were verified against Wikipedia's current officeholder lists on 2026-10-13.
replacement: Resolved Oct 23, 2026 (research-offices-sourced-parameters): the 60 rows were each checked against a fetched page (each office's Ballotpedia page, or the state's or territory's official site, with Wikipedia once for the U.S. Virgin Islands Board of Education roster), and each row in data/research/offices/statewide-executive-parties-2026.json now carries its page, a quote and the holder on January 20, 2025 and January 1, 2026. 54 matched; 6 were corrected (Arizona's lieutenant governor and the Northern Marianas' are partisan-ballot offices, Guam's attorney general is nonpartisan, the Virgin Islands boards of education and elections print party labels, and the Georgia labor commissioner's seat was vacant on the opening day). Read by statewidePartyOf in src/core2/offices-state.ts, which seats each office's party at the opening. Original replacement: Every row checked against Ballotpedia's partisan composition pages or the state's own records.

holds_back: A world candidate who campaigns harder because they know a rival stands ahead (an incumbent coming home to campaign) is kept as a steppedUp row and a campaign-stepped-up event, and the extra doors and hours reach voters, but no scene, journal line or news story tells it yet.
replacement: The director's scene or news line of a candidate stepping up their campaign, read from the campaign-stepped-up event and its steppedUp row by id (words session).

holds_back: Everyone in the line of succession to the presidency is taken to be a natural-born citizen and 14 years a resident; only the age of 35 is checked.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE: citizenship at birth and years of residence on a person's record; the line then passes over anyone who fails U.S. Const. art. II, sec. 1, cl. 5.

holds_back: The end of each term in progress at the opening for state and local offices: the seats of a body take turns over the years in one term that the office's calendar (the county schedule or the state's municipal election law) holds elections, and each term ends on the start day after its seat's election; where a state's own start rule isn't read, January 1 (the governors' clauses of AK, CA, CO, DE, FL, HI, IL, IN, LA, MD, ME, NJ, OH, OK, PA, VA, WA and WI, and, as estimates from the usual clause and the current governor's date, AZ, CT, GA, ID, KS, MN, MT, NE, NV, OR, TX, UT, VT and WY are read, in data/elections/term-starts.json). Federal terms are read: every House seat ends January 3 of an odd year (amend. XX), Senate seats by their real class, the presidency on January 20.
replacement: Oct 23, 2026 (research-offices-sourced-parameters): every place's governor clause (the mayor's for D.C.) and the day its legislators take their seats are now read into src/core2/data/elections/term-starts.json, with the URL and quoted text of each (48 governor rows and 43 legislature rows SOURCED; 8 and 13 ESTIMATED where the text sets no day and an inauguration or session date stands in, or, for Florida, Hawaii and Tennessee, where the text starts the term on election day itself and ruleStartAfter, which takes the first start after election day, uses the day after: one day late). Still open: municipal offices, whose start day is each charter's or the state's municipal law's, and county offices where county-election-schedule-by-state.json has no row, still start on the table's default of January 1. Earlier text: The other states' governor start clauses and the state-legislature start days read into data/elections/term-starts.json, and municipal timing from the 92O baselines (county bodies are read: county-election-schedule-by-state.json).

holds_back: An island area's state-level government has no spending or revenue by function in the data (Census state finances cover the states and D.C.). Its budget takes the states' residents-weighted function mix, scaled to the area's own all-funds spending a resident where published (Guam, the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico) and to the median of those where not (American Samoa, the Northern Marianas), with revenue equal to spending.
replacement: Each island area's published budget by function and its revenue by source (Guam, Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico budget documents; American Samoa and the Northern Marianas' Office of Insular Affairs financial reports) in public-budget-bases.json.

holds_back: A territory's governor race outside the town's own is not run, so its governor serves on past the election its law holds (Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands elect one in November 2026).
replacement: Superseded Oct 30, 2026 by SG-GOV-territory-legislature-race (gov-every-state-and-town-governs U1): governorRaces is deleted and another place's governor is raced through racesIn's one seat loop in src/core2/modules/voting.ts, whose territory check skips a territory's governor with its legislative and statewide executive seats under that row; the replacement (each territory's electorate places from its own governor, legislative or delegate results, and its own parties, on the same counted engine) is that row's.

holds_back: Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Marianas and the U.S. Virgin Islands have no legislative-district geography or member roster in the data, so each chamber's recorded seats are all elected at large by the whole territory.
replacement: Each territory's districts and sitting members, read from the territory's election commission, so seats are elected by district and hold the real parties and names.

holds_back: A territory's legislative seats, governor and statewide executive seats outside the town (Puerto Rico's, Guam's, the Virgin Islands', American Samoa's and the Northern Marianas') are not raced, in the world races or a legislative special election, so their opening holders serve on past the elections their law holds (Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands elect a governor in November 2026); a legislative vacancy there is filled by the offices engine's stand-in.
replacement: Each territory's electorate places from its own legislative, executive or delegate results, and its own parties on the count, so its seats are raced on the same counted engine (the same replacement as SG-GOV-territory-governor-race).

holds_back: A world candidate whose newest record of the race is word of a rival's message (an ad, a mailer or an evening of doors; a rivalWord row) reads where their race stands as how warm the people they know in town are to that rival against how warm they are to them (each impression's warmth, none where cold or unreached, averaged over the circle): their circle's actual warmth to both, not what those people said to the candidate.
replacement: A record of what the people a candidate talks to tell them about the race (who they have heard of, who they lean to), read by raceReading in place of the circle's recognition.

holds_back: Where the state's law settles an exact election tie by lot (about 34 states for general elections, 51 for primaries), the game holds a second election between the tied candidates instead.
replacement: RESOLVED (owner, Oct 14, 2026: ties follow the law of the state, a recorded lot where the law says lot): src/core2/election-ties.ts draws the lot from a stable hash of the contest and the tied candidates and keeps it as a tie record (citation, tied candidates, each slip, the result).

holds_back: A member of a deciding body who is a named official the world has not filled in as a person has no recorded views, so their party's side stands in for their lean when they vote on a tie.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE: a filled-in person for each official the moment they decide something, with their own views. Done Oct 15 (claude/elections-tie-named-member-lean): a member the world has not seated as a person is filled in by holderOf the moment they decide, and votes from their recorded views (officialLean); a member with no record at all abstains.

holds_back: Where a state's tie rule depends on race size (a new election for a large race, a lot for a small one) and its data row names no statute number, the line between them: 1,000 votes cast. North Carolina's row reads its statute's 5,000 (G.S. 163-182.8); no other state's row has a size rule yet.
replacement: The statute's size line in data/research/elections/tie-rules-2026.json. Built Oct 16: a small-race rule must carry the statute's own line (atOrBelowVotes); the 1,000-vote estimate and its parameter are deleted.

holds_back: A town hall's room, a candidate's forum among them, fills only from the town's full adults (townHallDrives reads townAdults): a resident still in the counted wider population never comes, so a forum in a town of mostly counted residents meets only the people already filled in.
replacement: townHallDrives reads the town's counted adults by the same drive as commentSpeakers does (countedResidents with countedRecordOnly), indexed by place so a weekly town hall does not scan the whole wider population, and holdTownHall fills in each counted resident who comes before the room's causes are written.

holds_back: A township board's ordinances are written as the town's own local law (the place level of the law chain), and a township board only legislates where no town council does; the law chain has no township level, so a township's ordinances and a village council's inside it can't both stand.
replacement: A township level in the law chain (laws-starting.ts) with its own starting law and enactments, so a township board and a village council inside it each legislate for their own jurisdiction.

holds_back: Election-day weather adds nothing to any voter's cost of voting: every election day is fair weather.
replacement: Retired the unsupported weather reason. A future weather effect requires an actual place-and-day weather record, with the same reader for named, counted, and wider voters.

holds_back: Whoever fills a seat the offices engine keeps no term for (another state's member of Congress, whom the officials engine seats from the roster) sits in the party of the one they replace: an appointee or a special election's winner is assumed to keep the seat's party. Since gov-every-state-and-town-governs U1 (Oct 29) every other place's chambers, governor and statewide executives are held on office terms, so their vacancies go through the offices engine's own fill, not this one.
replacement: Other states' seats in Congress held on office terms like every other seat, so the appointing authority's choice or the special election's result (the voting engine's world races) names the holder and their party.

holds_back: A mayor's veto is overridden by two thirds of the members voting; ordinances take effect 30 days after enactment.
replacement: Override majorities and ordinance effective dates from each state's municipal code and sampled charters, with estimates for the rest. Resolved by OPUS-GOV, Oct 12: two thirds of each body's whole membership (vetoOverrideShare, sourced in FIXER's stand-in figures).

holds_back: A person's opening stance on a policy question is their lean times the question's measured left-right axis, plus, for the eight questions the CES 2020 has an item for, a stored opening record with its reasons (src/core2/modules/views.ts openingRecord, data/research/people/opening-stance-loadings.json) holding what their faith and four-year degree add beyond the lean. Every other question, and every person with no recorded faith or schooling, opens as the lean alone, and no trait loading exists because the CES has no personality measure.
replacement: Per-question opening records for the questions the survey did not ask (a source with loadings for each), until every question opens as a stored record formed from the person's life.

holds_back: In a nonpartisan or local race, voters the world doesn't name vote as lean bands around the place's lean, sized from the town's population times the 2024 share of people who voted, each band voting with its named people. (Partisan state and federal races now count them in blocks: src/core2/electorate-blocks.ts.) The figures are researched: 0.46 of residents vote on a presidential date, scaled by cycle (midterm 0.72, off-cycle 0.39; Hajnal and Green 2024); what stays a stand-in is the local groups themselves.
