replacement: CORE's populated voter groups (counts by place, age, job and household, with lean and turnout), each voting as a group.

holds_back: Every adult resident counts as a registered voter where filing or signing requires registration.
replacement: Retired the unsupported registered-voter eligibility result. Age, residence, deadlines, party membership and term limits remain separate checks. Reintroduce a registration mechanic only if the owner or golden path calls for it, with actual records.

holds_back: On a minimum wage's effective date the laws module replaces each underpaid work commitment's hourly rate directly in core work state.
replacement: OPUS-CORE's work pay-change API (re-rate a commitment from a date with its source), called here instead. Resolved 2026-10-13: Replaced by OPUS-CORE's rerateJob (core2-api-v12) in laws.ts raiseOne and raiseToFloor; counted residents' jobs rise too.

holds_back: A council seat chosen by part of town counts only the voters of its part: the town's households in their recorded order are cut into equal runs, one per seat chosen that way, and the counted residents and the rest of the town divide equally among them. No part of town has a boundary or a street behind it.
replacement: Council districts drawn from the town's dwellings (by the council or a commission, to near equal population as its charter says), each household and each sitting member placed by their dwelling.

holds_back: A candidate for a council seat chosen by part of town must live in that part of town. The rule is assumed for every place: no charter text the repository holds says whether its ward or district seats ask it, and the part of town is the household-order ward of SG-GOV-ward-map.
replacement: Read each place's charter or state law for whether a ward or district candidate must live in it, and apply the check only where it does; the part of town then comes from the dwellings, as SG-GOV-ward-map's replacement draws it.

holds_back: When filing closes, a statewide partisan race with no candidate of one major party gets that party's nominee: a named official, or a person filled in to run for it.
replacement: PEOPLE's who-runs decisions file each candidate through fileCandidacy with recorded reasons; incumbents decide the same way.

holds_back: Wider races reach named officials across their jurisdiction and the played town residents: a state race, the state's officials and serving holders; a national race, every member of Congress, the town's own state's officials and every place's governor and statewide officers (another place's are filled in from their term rows the first time a national pool is built, fillStatewideHolders in src/core2/candidate-pool.ts), but not another place's legislators, who stay named on their terms (SG-GOV-outside-legislators-national-pool). Unnamed ordinary residents elsewhere have no candidate records. State legislative district residency is not individually known for officials stored at state scope.
replacement: Jurisdiction-wide counted household records with district membership, using the same candidacy reasons before filling in a runner.

holds_back: Another state's governor race is run on the counted engine and its winner's party is kept on the seat from the state's inauguration day, but no engine acts as that state's executive: no budget, signature or appointment there reads the new governor, and the officials roster keeps the governor seated at the opening.
replacement: Resolved Oct 30, 2026 (gov-every-state-and-town-governs U1, the laws lead's decision B): every other state's governor is held on the offices engine's term from the opening (seatOutsideOffices in src/core2/modules/offices.ts), and racesIn's one seat loop in src/core2/modules/voting.ts races the governor's seat by the same rule as every other statewide office (governorRaces is deleted), so seatRaceWinner seats the winner on that term through seatWinner, the one term writer, at home in that state; the voting engine's own seats table is no longer written for a governor, and the race reads the incumbent's party from the serving term. The officials roster's separate governor is gone. A coarse executive acting for each other state (budget, signature, appointment) is the world-governing plan's U3 (SG-GOV-other-legislatures-not-sitting).

holds_back: A race the town doesn't vote in is counted on the counted residents' engine at a coarser level (a House district's, the state's counties', a legislative district's eligible voters, voting as the town's counted residents would on each place's 2024 lean), but its candidates are each party's typical candidate (the holder stands for their party with the typical campaign) rather than people with records, and a state legislative district with no read result is the state's vote over its districts leaning to its holder's party at the typical margin.
replacement: Each race's candidates as fictional people with records and campaigns, and each legislative district's own 2024 result.

holds_back: Each group-quarters type's residents are aged and sexed from a TUNABLE profile (src/core2/data/people/group-quarters.json: age bands with shares, each checked against plus or minus 0.10, and a female share with its own spread), split by largest remainder with ages spread evenly across each band. Other noninstitutional quarters start at 16: a shelter's younger children live there with a parent, which a room of residents of one sex cannot hold.
replacement: The 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics tables PCO3 to PCO10 (group quarters population by sex and age for each major type, national level), fetched by a researcher and read in place of the TUNABLE shares (SOURCED).

holds_back: Group-quarters room records are doors a campaign knocks on (src/core2/campaign-day.ts): a canvasser reaches a prison cell or a nursing-home room like a house.
replacement: Skip institutional rooms as doors (a dormitory may stay one where a campus allows canvassing); governing lead (pool item gov-group-quarters-electorate).

holds_back: Each place's group-quarters count by type is the 2020 Census's, on April 1, 2020 (during the pandemic, college students counted at their campus housing), applied to a world that opens years later and scaled only by the world's population against the published one.
replacement: A later vintage of P5 when one is published, or the ACS group-quarters tables by type for places when published, read in place of the 2020 row.

holds_back: Counted residents of adult correctional facilities vote at the town's counted scale (src/core2/modules/voting.ts, countedScale and the counted voter loops) like any other counted adult, and may be drawn to run for a local seat (src/core2/modules/candidacy.ts, countedScreen). The state's barred share of the counted electorate still covers prisoners on average (src/core2/law-reach/group-a-voting.ts), but not concentrated in a prison town.
replacement: Skip counted correctional residents in the counted voter loops unless the state's law lets incarcerated people vote (incarceratedMayVote, src/core2/justice-law.ts), take the prison part out of the state's barred share, and leave them out of the counted candidacy draw; governing lead's chain (pool item gov-group-quarters-electorate).

holds_back: The opening's employment target reads each county's ACS employment rate by age (employed over civilians 16 and over, B23001) over the town's residents outside institutions and military quarters, though the county's civilians include its own institutional residents: in a county with many of them (a prison county) the town's target is low by their share of each age row.
replacement: Each county's employed over its civilian noninstitutional population by age (ACS PUMS, or B23001 less the county's institutional residents by age from the 2020 Census DHC), read in place of the B23001 rate.

holds_back: A group-quarters room group's property-crime exposure reads as an owner's (src/core2/modules/crime.ts, a tenure other than rent reads as own), and institutional residents count in the town's exposure to violent crime like any household.
replacement: The National Crime Victimization Survey's universe (households and noninstitutional residents) for exposure, with institutions' own incidents apart.

holds_back: The jobs engine keeps full residents of institutions and military quarters out of civilian work as the counted tier does (outOfCivilianWork, src/core2/modules/jobs.ts), and staff candidates now read the same rule (src/core2/modules/staff.ts, roomOutsideLaborForce), but seating a public post (src/core2/public-payroll.ts) reads custody only: a resident of a nursing home or a barracks, full or counted, may be seated in a public post.
replacement: Public posts read the household's group-quarters type as the jobs engine does (outsideLaborForce), once the seating of elected and appointed officials who live in such a room is ruled on, or a custody record for a correctional resident.

holds_back: A filled-in group-quarters resident's home is drawn as a house: a room's kind (its type) has no picture, so homePlaceFor shows a suburban house (src/bench/backdrop-places.ts), and the person card reads the room as rented with its type's name.
replacement: Dormitory, cell, barracks and nursing-room backdrops (asset-scene-admission) and the card's own label for a room; People v4 and the play-first lane.

holds_back: No group-quarters resident pays for their room: a college's room and board, a prison's per diem and a nursing home's rate are not billed to anyone. Residents of institutions spend nothing in town and hold no cash; college, military and other noninstitutional residents keep one person's CES nonhousing costs each.
replacement: The institution's own books: a college bills room and board, a nursing home bills its residents or Medicaid, a prison is paid by its government, and the residents' costs move through them.

holds_back: Only college and nursing-home rooms name the institution that houses them (the town's college directory record, its nursing-home employer); a prison's, a juvenile facility's, a base's and other institutions' rooms name none.
replacement: Prison, base and other institution records in the town, named on their rooms' dwellings.

holds_back: Residents of juvenile facilities aged 5 to 17 count as the town's public-school students and seniors (src/core2/school-outcomes.ts).
replacement: The facility's own schooling, outside the town's public schools.

holds_back: Law reach (src/core2/counted-reach.ts, src/core2/law-reach/group-b-people.ts) and the poverty count (src/core2/world-poverty.ts) read zero-income group-quarters room records as poor households: an inmate or a nursing-home resident reads as eligible and as poor. A room's counted group is keyed to the income fifth its zero or student income reads as (src/core2/modules/residents.ts, groupKeyOf); the jobs, health and births webs read no fifth for a room.
replacement: The Census poverty universe (no institutional, military or college-dormitory residents) for the poverty count, and each program's own eligibility for law reach; laws lead (pool item laws-group-quarters-means-tests).

holds_back: Service members in military quarters have no job and no pay: they are outside the civilian labor force, so the opening gives them no civilian job and no share of the unplaced pay, and nothing pays them as service members.
replacement: An outside armed-forces payer that pays service members in military quarters at military pay by rank and years.

holds_back: Institutions admit no one: group-quarters rooms take no newcomers and lose no one to the households' leaving rates, counted or full (src/core2/modules/counted-moves.ts skips counted rooms; src/core2/modules/moves.ts keeps full residents of rooms out of the monthly review and every booked review), so deaths and fill-ins lower each type's count and students and service members age in place year after year.
replacement: A yearly intake through admitCountedHousehold that holds each type at its research row: a college admits a class each fall, a prison and a nursing home admit as residents leave (pool item core-group-quarters-turnover), needed before long saves.

holds_back: In a place with noninstitutional group quarters, the households' unplaced workers earn the place's median earnings (ACS B20002) blended toward the town's median recorded wage by the place's share in noninstitutional group quarters: (1 - s) times the place's figure plus s times the recorded median, s the Census count in college, military and other noninstitutional quarters over the published population (the place's figure as it is where the town records no wage). The civilian residents of its rooms are a pool apart, paid the place's figure as it is.
replacement: Household residents' earnings from the ACS Public Use Microdata Sample for the place's PUMA (people not in group quarters), read in place of the blend.

holds_back: Every group-quarters room record holds groupQuartersRoomMembers residents (2, TUNABLE, spread 1 to 4) of the same sex in age order, whatever its type: a dormitory double, a two-person cell, a barracks room and a nursing-home room alike.
replacement: Each type's sourced occupancy where one exists (campus housing's rooms per resident, a prison's cells, a base's barracks), read per type.

holds_back: Each member's medical bill starts from the household's Consumer Expenditure average split evenly over its members, moved only by their care need and their coverage: age is not read (MEPS Statistical Brief #441: average out-of-pocket "ranging from $283 for children under age 18 to $1,215 for the elderly"), the uninsured use as much care as the insured at the same need (MEPS #441: 55.4 percent of the uninsured under 65 had any expense against 88.1 percent of the privately insured), and a counted member's care need is one while a counted illness runs and none otherwise (counted people hold no condition record), while a full member's held conditions raise it on the health engine's sliding scale. A counted household keeps back only its group's housing arrears, where a full household keeps back the housing due before the next bill. Only households in the places whose money the world keeps (the residents runtime's places: the town and the places around it) are billed and counted in the care norm; a household elsewhere, such as a national press outlet's head or a central-bank governor, who keeps no books, is never billed.
replacement: An age profile of out-of-pocket spending (MEPS by age band) and the uninsured's lower use of care at the same need, as parameters the bill reads; counted members' condition prevalence from the condition pack's cells, so a counted member's care need follows the same sliding scale; the counted keep-back from the housing payments each group owes before the next bill. When a household outside those places keeps books (a national figure's pay and living costs), it is billed by its own place's region on the same rule.

holds_back: A medical bill unpaid past the wait is placed for collection as one balance on the household's books and stays there: no collector pays the provider for it, the household never pays it down or settles it, and the part the web's share does not send to collections is written off by the provider with no record. Each part leaves the credit report seven years after its own delinquency and is folded into the record's agedOff summary, still owed: the balance never ages off the books. The bank reads it as a charge-off once the reporting wait has passed (creditMedicalReportDays), with no floor for small balances.
replacement: Medical debts paid down from what a household holds after its living costs, on the same rule as its other debts, settled or sold at research's recovery rates, and the provider's write-off kept as its charity care on its books.

holds_back: A counted household's medical-bill row holds what one real household of it still owes the provider, standing for its whole weight. When the household is filled in, the new full household keeps that row by its id (one household's owed bills), and the records that take the rest of its weight (counted-groups.ts releaseWeight) keep only their own: the owed bills of the other households it stood for leave no record, never reach collections and are written off by no one.
replacement: At fill-in, the owed bills of the households released from the record move to the records that take their weight, in proportion to the weight each takes, by the same rule that moves the group's living-cost arrears (world-fill-in-strands-group-living-arrears).

holds_back: coverage-to-mortality-55-64 cuts a full person's death hazard at 55 to 64 by their own Medicaid coverage, and job-loss-to-death-risk raises it for a worker whose long job ended in a closure or layoff (src/core2/health-own.ts, src/core2/job-displacement.ts), and long-hours-to-heart-and-stroke raises it for a worker whose job is recorded at long weekly hours. A counted person has none of these records of their own (the law reach keeps the town's counted adults' Medicaid coverage by person id, but the counted flows do not read it for illness; they read no closure and no job hours), so the counted flows (src/core2/births-counted.ts) keep the place-level twin, medicaid-expansion-to-mortality, which is the same cause averaged over the low-income 55- to 64-year-olds enrolled or not, and take no job-loss or long-hours excess. The research finds the excess only at firms that lost 30% or more of their jobs; the jobs engine keeps no firm peak, so a layoff counts when it reaches a worker with years on the job, which it lets go only after everyone it values less (a deep cut), and a worker's sex is not split although the paper's sample is men.
replacement: The counted flows read the law reach's coverage records (medicaidCoverageSpells, by person id) and multiply a counted member's chance of a serious illness by the same (1 + size x covered) / (1 + size x covered at the first look) factor, leaving the place-level twin out for them as for a full person; the counted flows read the jobs engine's closure records (the changes table, counted workers included) and the counted jobs' hours, and multiply a displaced or long-hours counted member's chance by the same excess.

holds_back: Each full teen's monthly past-month cannabis use record (and the counted teens' count in the counted monthly row) is decided from their own conscientiousness and the place's share, which the state's sales law moves through the outcome web, but no other engine reads the record yet: a teen who used is no different at school, at home or at 18.
replacement: The school engine reads a teen's use where it decides grades and leaving school, and the health engine reads it where a person turning 18 is given the adult substance-use condition, each at a researched size.

holds_back: A couple among people filled in from the counts is told from who shares a home and a child (two grown members of one household who are both kin to the child at home), because the counted columns record shared homes but not who is partnered; a couple with no child at home, or a household of several grown kin, is not told, and a former partner is never told.
replacement: Carry the partnership in the counted household record when the opening generates it, with the day it began, so fill-in reads it instead of inferring it.

holds_back: A move into the county before the start is dated by the moves engine's life-stage rate and the hold of children at home only: a lost job, owning a home, relatives in town and the person's own temperament, which push or hold in play, do not move it; whether someone came is read only from a parent living outside the county or a recorded birthplace outside it, so a person whose parents died long ago never came.
replacement: Run moves and the working life together, quarter by quarter, so a layoff pushes a move as the moves engine's work.job-lost pull does in play; record where each person grew up when the opening generates their family.

holds_back: The working life before the start runs in the person's day-one town, against its businesses' day-one size and going pay and the nation's unemployment rate; a spell before a person's move into the county runs where they lived then with no employer named (the world keeps none there), and officials living outside the town are not run.
replacement: the regional economy series in the economy pass, business sizes from the business pass's history, and history-past-officials for officials' careers.

holds_back: A school year in a place with no public school district record (a place the world does not keep, or a town whose opening has no police department to copy the district from) is recorded against the place's schools as the place itself, with no name, so the Journal, the person card and talk leave it out.
replacement: Every place a person can have lived keeps its schools at a coarser level (AGENTS.md: other places at a coarser level), each with a generated name from the place's records, and every town opens with its district.

holds_back: Counted people serving a jail, prison or juvenile term keep their pay: a counted case's custody is a head count by counted group (CountedCustodyRow), with no record of which member serves, so no counted member's job ends and no counted household loses an earner, as a named prisoner's household does (endCustodyJobs, parent-incarceration-to-household-income).
replacement: A record of which counted members a counted term holds, decided from their own records (the age band, the group's members and their jobs), so the jobs engine ends their jobs for the term as it does a named prisoner's, and the counted household's income loses that pay.

holds_back: A counted member's marital status and which relative is their child: a woman is married when an adult relative within the minimum parent age of her age lives in her household, and a mother when a relative under 5 is at least that much younger.
replacement: Counted members' partner and parent-child links kept in the counts, read in place of the age rule.

holds_back: defense-contracts-to-earnings does nothing: its cause federal.defense-boost-pct (extra defense contracts as a share of the state's output) is not recorded by any engine, so the link never runs; the pay level already reads labor.median-earnings and will carry it once the cause exists.
replacement: A federal spending engine recording each state's defense contract awards, read as federal.defense-boost-pct.

holds_back: minimum-wage-to-low-wage-jobs and federal-minimum-wage-to-low-wage-jobs scale only the staffing targets of employers the jobs engine reviews, and in played towns none of those has a job under the line; the town's low-wage jobs belong to organizations the review never reaches, so the factor moves no record.
replacement: The jobs engine applies the low-wage factor to every organization whose jobs labor.low-wage-jobs counts, at the moment it sets that organization's staffing, shown in a low-wage-only twin by employer id.

holds_back: The minimum-wage-to-low-wage-jobs link needs the minimum wage as a share of the place's median wage (labor.minimum-wage-to-median), which no engine records.
replacement: A reader in the jobs engine of the wage floor over the place's median hourly pay, added to the engine measures.

holds_back: Local immigration enforcement (enforcement-to-undocumented-employment, enforcement-to-us-born-employment) reaches workers through the jobs engine's pull to work, by a work authorization seeded on who each noncitizen is (isUnauthorized in src/core2/citizenship.ts), at one national share of noncitizens who are unauthorized (parameter unauthorizedShareOfNoncitizens, Pew 2024) rather than each state's. Citizens stand for the U.S.-born the research measures, since the core records no birthplace, so naturalized citizens take the U.S.-born effect. Only the pull to work reads it; no employer checks authorization at hire.
replacement: A per-state unauthorized share of noncitizens (Pew state estimates over ACS noncitizens, table B05001) in place data, and a seeded nativity on people (full and counted) so naturalized citizens are told from the U.S.-born.

holds_back: The size of the web's participation effects on mothers and married women at work, and of the pull to formal work of anyone the justice engine first held while they waited for a hearing (pretrial-detention-to-employment): the engine adds the log of the factor to a deterministic choice score, which reaches the records but is not fitted to the researched size. The older workers' term has its own fitted weight (jobsOlderWorkWebWeight).
replacement: A weight on the term, fitted in a played year so each group's share moves by the researched size (mothers, married women), as jobsOlderWorkWebWeight is for ages 62 to 66.

holds_back: Birth-year pollution (birth-year-pollution-to-adult-earnings), teacher quality (teacher-quality-to-earnings) and neighborhood years (neighborhood-years-to-adult-outcomes) acting on adult earnings move nothing, each for its own missing piece. Birth-year pollution: the exposure is on record for anyone born in play (a person:birth fact with place and date, src/core2/births-people.ts, and the web's month rows of env.particulates for that place), but no pay decision reads it and the link has no size. Teacher quality: nothing records a teacher's value-added or which teacher a student has, and no law or engine moves teacher value-added, so the cause has no producer and no policy to carry. Neighborhood years: where each person lived each year is on record (residenceOn in src/core2/past-moves.ts, and moves in play), but no data row holds a county's childhood exposure effect, no pay decision reads it and the link has no size.
replacement: Birth-year pollution: a read in src/core2/jobs-web.ts of the person's birth fact and the web's particulates over their birth year, sized from its study. Teacher quality: parked until a researched link moves teacher value-added (a teacher-pay or evaluation law); then the school engine keeps a value-added per teacher and a yearly classroom, and hirePay reads its mean. Neighborhood years: a county row of childhood exposure effects, read in hirePay from residenceOn and in-play moves.

holds_back: Pretrial detention lowering the pull to formal work (pretrial-detention-to-employment): the jobs engine adds the log of one plus the row's size to the choice score of anyone the justice engine first held while they waited for a hearing, from the row's lag on and for good. The research measures the gap three to four years after the hearing, not how long it lasts or whether a second detention adds to it, and every job the jobs engine keeps stands for formal employment because it keeps no informal work. A counted member carries no term: the justice engine files counted defendants as cases by group (CountedCaseRow, detained as a count), and the counts keep no record of which member was held.
replacement: A duration from the research on the term; a record of which counted member was held, for the counted tier to read as a named person's is; and the term fitted in a played year so detained defendants' share at work runs the researched 20% under that of those released (see SG-LABOR-participation-scale).

holds_back: A town resident's regional job is priced from the BLS OEWS wage for the occupation of the town role nearest to what they were paid (metro or state area, starting percentile, moved with the place's pay level). Where OEWS publishes no wage for that occupation, the town's own nearest role sets the pay. The occupation is the town role's, not the person's own job history.
replacement: Keep the occupation of the last job on the seeker row and price the regional job from it.

holds_back: Transit loss to unemployment (transit-loss-to-unemployment), broadband to employment (broadband-to-employment), incentive deals to industry jobs (incentive-deal-to-industry-jobs) and more immigrants to the workforce (more-immigration-to-workforce) have no researched size the game can use, and a Medicaid work requirement's effect on employment (work-requirement-to-employment) is about zero, so an engine would multiply by one.
replacement: Sizes confirmed from the sources and the cause measures (transit access, deal records) recorded by their engines.

holds_back: The social media age check law reaches a teen's mood through the youth gap in their resting stress: for a person aged 13 to 17 (socialMediaAgeFrom up to the voting age, the law's reach row), the age-gap term of restingStress (restingStressYouthWeight, the PSS-10 gap between ages 14 to 19 and adults) is multiplied by the outcome web's factor on health.youth-major-depressive-episode (age-verification-to-youth-depressive-episode), one for one with the share of teens in a major depressive episode. The whole youth gap is treated as the part of a teen's stress that tracks that share. No teen has a mood, depression or social media use record: the person's stress baseline moves for every teen in a place alike (the factor is the place's, not the person's own use), and the measure is the survey's 12 to 17 band applied to the law's 13 to 17. The link's size is an estimate from Australia's under-16 account drop, college-age studies of Facebook and of cutting social media, and a normal-threshold conversion to the share in an episode (data/research/outcome-web/links.json).
replacement: The health engine keeps an adolescent depression condition per full teen (and a count for counted teens) decided from the teen's own traits, home and use, calibrated to the NSDUH share in an episode (health.youth-major-depressive-episode), with the web's factor multiplying that rate where the health engine decides it; a teen's social media use becomes a free-time act the age check removes for the teens it reaches; resting stress then reads the condition instead of scaling the age gap.

holds_back: A state that adopts an estate or inheritance tax by a bill that sets only a rate (it had none, so the bill has no schedule to keep) taxes the whole estate or share at that rate, with no exemption and no classes of heirs.
replacement: An adopting bill carries a schedule (an exemption, and for an inheritance tax the classes of heirs), drafted from the states that levy the tax.

holds_back: A counted heir's relation to the person who died is read from the years between them (a parent's age younger, a child; older, a parent; nearer, the partner), so a counted sibling is taxed as a partner; and the estate is the dead person's share of their household's cash (the counts pool it in the group's account), not their own assets. A counted estate no one inherits is assessed against the state as heir, but a tax on that heir (where a statute taxes a government; none of the starting law's five does) is recorded as assessed and not collected, because the retired household's cash has left the pool.
replacement: The counted store keeps each family pair's kind (partner, child, parent, sibling) and each member's own assets, read for the estate and the inheritance class.

holds_back: A government that takes an estate no one else does is assumed exempt from the state's inheritance tax where the law row carries no researched statute term for it: a state that adopts an inheritance tax by a bill (the bill sets a rate, not the statute's exemptions), and Kentucky, whose statute exempts transfers to cities, towns and public institutions in the state for public purposes without naming the Commonwealth itself, so the Commonwealth taking an estate by escheat is our reading of it. Maryland, Nebraska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania name the state itself and are quoted in data.
replacement: A statute-cited governmentHeir term on every inheritance-tax row: an adopting bill carries its state's term (the engine taxes the government at the state's rate for others when the term says exempt: false), and Kentucky's Department of Revenue or a court confirms the Commonwealth is exempt as an escheat taker.

holds_back: A bill the committee chair holds without a hearing keeps the chair's reasons on the committee record (their position on the bill, part by part, and what their temperament adds toward a hearing), but no scene, story or later decision reads them yet.
replacement: The sponsor-asks-chair scene and the held-bill press line read the chair's reasons by the committee record's id (laws-hold-record-names-the-sponsor).

holds_back: The immigration partnership moves the web's Hispanic school enrollment, undocumented employment and U.S.-born employment, but no school or jobs engine reads those measures.
replacement: WORLD and PEOPLE: school enrollment and jobs engines read the kept measures when they enroll and hire.

holds_back: The class of minor offenses the case flow models (disorderly conduct, drunkenness, liquor law violations, loitering and vagrancy) leaves out drug possession, and its police-staffing link takes the elasticity Chalfin, Hansen, Weisburst and Williams measured for a quality-of-life group that includes drug possession.
replacement: The owner's ruling on where drug possession arrests sit (docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md), built as a second stream in the case flow with its own FBI arrest rate by state and the same police link.

holds_back: The named residents' share of ordinary-crime arrests is carried in an unnamed batch of cases; no named person is arrested, held or sentenced by this engine.
replacement: PEOPLE and GOV: an act engine where a named person's drives, record and circumstances decide an offense, then the case flow charges them from that act.

holds_back: The web's youth firearm death and suicide rates become an expected count of young people lost in the town each month, but no named child dies of it.
replacement: PEOPLE: an injury death for full and counted young people, booked from this expected count.

holds_back: The state's grant of local income-tax authority is read and recorded when a local body drafts an income-tax bill, and a state law row can grant or withdraw it, but no body can propose, enact or repeal the grant by bill.
replacement: Resolved Oct 28: the bill catalog offers law:local-income-tax-authority to state chambers (scripts/research/build-bill-catalog.py), worded by the Words row from #6432, so a legislature grants or withdraws its towns' power to tax income by bill and a town's next income-tax bill reads the law in force.

holds_back: The laws listed in outcome-research-gaps.json (each with the outcome its research would measure) move no outcome-web measure: no researched link starts from the law or from a measure an engine sets from it, so the web holds those outcomes at their base whatever the law does.
replacement: A researched link per law in links.json (strength, shape, lag, source), built by the outcome-web line, after which each row leaves outcome-research-gaps.json.

holds_back: The federal share of public assistance once Congress has states share disaster costs is the 50 percent FEMA's head said was coming (May 15, 2025, Reuters), spread 25 to 75 percent (disasterFederalShareWhenStatesShare); no enacted bill sets it. The cut applies to the federal public assistance the declaration pays the county and town governments.
replacement: The share from the first enacted or introduced text, with the state's own cost taken up by the state government's budget.

holds_back: Six federal questions (the debt limit, immigration levels, student loan forgiveness, D.C. statehood, federal mandatory minimums, the members' stock trading ban) start as law in force ('no', each cited) and Congress can enact or repeal them from the bill paper, but no engine reads the law, so enacting one moves no money, person or place. National data privacy is read now: the business engine charges employing businesses a compliance cost while it stands (federal-data-privacy-law.test.ts). The disaster cost share is read now (disasters.ts).
replacement: One reader per question, each from its research (data/research/campaigns/federal-questions-2026.json names the cheapest reader for each), so enacting the law changes a record another engine reads.

holds_back: A state's grocery exemption spares groceries from every level's sales tax in the town, as if every state's local sales taxes followed the state's base. A county's or city's exemption spares only its own tax.
replacement: A per-state field in the starting-law research (data/research/laws/local-starting-law/sales-tax.json) saying whether local sales taxes follow the state's grocery exemption, sourced from each state's revenue department, read here so a state exemption spares only the levels its base covers.

holds_back: A lobbying ban with no numeric period on its law row retains the existing estimated two-year cooling-off period. Researched numeric periods are read from the actual law instead.
replacement: Supply the missing structured periods through researched starting-law and voted bill provisions; remove the fallback when every applicable ban carries one.

holds_back: How big a gap between a member's wanted budget line and the line in force must be before they file a mid-year amendment (1 percent of the line, spread 0.5 to 3 percent, budgetAmendmentMinShare) is an estimate; no table of local amendment thresholds was found. Real councils also take up contracts, appointments and rezonings that no record here carries.
replacement: Thresholds from sampled local budget-amendment codes and agendas.

holds_back: A bordering state's law on a question, which weighs on a state legislator's reason to carry the same change (neighborLawWeight), is that state's researched starting law, not its law in force: only the town's state legislates in a played world, so no other state's own acts are recorded and a neighbor never changes its law.
replacement: Read each bordering state's law in force from the laws a coarse state legislature enacts for it, so a neighbor's change reaches its neighbors the next session.

holds_back: The state-chamber party-loyalty weight (weights.statePartyLoyalty, 1) is checked against the federal party-unity figure (about 0.90, CQ Vote Studies) because the state roll-call calibration input is not in the repository.
replacement: Run the owner's state roll-call input against the simulated chambers (src/core2/party-loyalty.test.ts measures them), set statePartyLoyalty and the test's target from it, and close this row.

holds_back: Cosponsors are recorded only for the bill the played official sponsors; other members' bills carry none.
replacement: Record cosponsors for every full person's bill from the same rule, once the position read is cheap enough, and fold the counted members' signatures as a count.

holds_back: A budget-line section that names its own effective date (provisionFor with an effectiveDate) is amended into the budget the day the bill becomes law: amendBudget takes no date, so every step of a budget phase-in would land at once; seatAct refuses phase-in steps on a budget line for that reason.
replacement: The budgets engine amends a line on the section's date: enact schedules the dated budget section on the calendar (as enactLaw does a dated law row) and amendBudget applies it to the fiscal year that date falls in, so lawmakers and the budget screen read each step when it lands; seatAct then takes phase-in steps on a budget line, as it does on a law amount.

holds_back: A bill drafted from the seat phases in an amount only by dated steps the sponsor names (one section per step). The ruling's other form, an amount that rises by a percent a year, cannot be drafted: the seat takes no rate and no span.
replacement: seatAct takes a percent a year and the years it runs; the steps are drafted as dated sections of the one bill a year apart, each the law in force raised by the percent, through the same enact path (or one indexed law row the laws engine raises each year on its calendar), with no number typed.

holds_back: How much a letter from a relative elsewhere weighs, so that a close tie's letter ranks among the year's top moments.
replacement: A measured weight of family contact in the life-change literature, or the people engine's own appraisal of the contact.

holds_back: A relative or acquaintance living elsewhere (the inactive tier) never moves into the played town: their move skips a relative or county destination that is one of the town's full-detail places and goes to the next record instead.
replacement: A husk whose move lands in the played town arrives through the counted-moves arrival path as one counted household (one model, two tiers), filled in when the player meets them.

holds_back: Relatives elsewhere write in proportion to closeness alone; the writer's traits (a letter writer or not) do not move how often.
replacement: A trait-decision row for keeping in touch with a relative elsewhere, weighed against the month's typical like the partnering pull.

holds_back: Every partnership formed in play is recorded as a marriage (union: married); nobody moves in together unmarried.
replacement: NSFG cohabitation and transition-to-marriage paces by age, so a union starts as cohabiting or married and a cohabitation marries or ends at its own pace.

holds_back: The counted population's household types never change by partnering or parting.
replacement: people-partnership-counted (with its parts people-partnership-counted-leave-home and people-partnership-counted-pair-and-split): the counted households partner and part by partneringPerYear and separatingPerYear times their count, merging and splitting counted households.

holds_back: A partner met by someone living elsewhere is always of the other sex: no adult carries a recorded orientation, so the pairing cannot read one (owner, Oct 19: "who pairs with whom reads each person's own record, including orientation"; #4963's woman-and-man pairing was ruled a defect).
replacement: people-orientation-record: every adult carries a recorded orientation, and the partner met is of a sex both records admit, with the ACS share of same-sex couples (about 1.5%) and their age gaps checking totals.

holds_back: A couple in the played town climbs dating, living together, engaged and married on set stage lengths (partnerDatingMonths, partnerLivingTogetherMonths, partnerEngagedMonths), moved by the pair's traits; a single whose pull is full and who knows nobody fitting meets a partner from the wider population who already shares their home.
replacement: NSFG/ACS transition paces by age and union duration (dating to living together, living together to marrying or ending), and the meetings engine bringing singles together so a fitting partner is known before the pull is full.

holds_back: A relative or town leaver living elsewhere works, is let go, finds work and moves to another job with no employer named: the world keeps no firms outside the played town.
replacement: The regional engine's employers by industry for each state (counted, never named until met) give a person living elsewhere an employer record their work spell names, filled in when the player meets it.

holds_back: Someone living elsewhere who was out of the labor force on day one (a student, a parent at home, someone not looking) stays out until they reach the age of retiring.
replacement: The jobs engine's enter choice (the one counted and full people make) read for people living elsewhere from their age, household and partner's work, checked against CPS flows into the labor force by age.

holds_back: What a household keeps back for its next rent or mortgage before buying everyday living counts the members' gross daily wage until the payment is due; the payroll's withholding is not netted out, so a household whose take-home pay barely covers its home keeps back a little too little.
replacement: The members' take-home pay due before the next living day, from the payroll's withholding (withholdingFor, src/core2/tax-withholding.ts) or the pay last received, read by housingKeptBack in src/core2/cost-of-living.ts.

holds_back: A sitting president or governor at home is shown outside the White House or the governor's residence by day and in the large house's living room at night, because neither residence has painted rooms.
replacement: Painted rooms for each residence (white-house-residence-living, -dining, -bedroom; governor-residence-living, -dining, -bedroom), imported under those names.

holds_back: Old smooth family-plan coefficients; living-cost and household-size housing proxies, recorded affect health proxy, identity gender carrier proxy, successful planned singleton pregnancy with fixed conception-relative duration, infant inactive discretionary tier until future development work.
replacement: Researched Oct 24, 2026 (research-people-sourced-parameters): renewalGestationDays SOURCED at 268 days from ovulation (Jukic and others, Human Reproduction 2013); renewalAgeCenter 30.0 and renewalAgeSpread 8.7 years ESTIMATED from the NCHS 2024 fertility schedule (data/research/renewal/natality-2024.json); renewalTimingPeakYears 2.25 ESTIMATED from NCHS Data Brief 240 (2016); renewalMedianAnnualIncomeMinor ESTIMATED from the HUD FY2025 income limits every other place reads; all checked by scripts/research/people-parameters-check.ts and read by birthCircumstances in src/core2/births-plan.ts and birthStanding in src/core2/births-counted.ts. Still open: the 14 weights and pulls have no convertible source (the plan is a utility-max choice, and no study publishes its coefficients), so they stay TUNABLE and the town's births per 1,000 women 15 to 44 are reported against the place's NCHS rate by scripts/research/people-year.ts; the 91-day review is a fixed step (people-renewal-renewalReviewDays-as-cause); each place's own age shape is people-births-age-shape-by-place. Source-matched individual reproductive/clinical records, dated pregnancy outcomes, dwelling capacity and coupled choice calibration; infant development producer. Finisher must review these limits against Part 1.

holds_back: Opening still-pregnant plans use current opening money, housing, health and temperament as pre-opening proxies, with real recorded partnership and child dates. Reviews occur at 91-day phases anchored to partnership or youngest child; both partners must agree through the chooser. No surveyed fertility rate decides pregnancy.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE dated lived pregnancy/resource/medical history, or a finisher/CTO accepted reconstruction with validated first-year calibration. Researched Oct 23, 2026 (research-core-sourced-parameters): the share of women 15 to 44 carrying a pregnancy to a live birth on a given day is the place's fertility rate (NCHS 2024, data/research/renewal/natality-2024.json, all 56 places; 53.8 per 1,000 nationally) times the median 268 days from ovulation to birth (Jukic et al., Human Reproduction, 2013): about 3.9% nationally and 2.2% to 5.7% across places, in data/research/core/opening-pregnancy-2024.json; scripts/research/core-year.ts reports a town's opening pregnancies against it. The rate checks the town and never decides who is pregnant. Still open: no dated pre-opening history; the builder item people-opening-pregnancy-first-year-calibration.

holds_back: A debate whose host outlet has no living reporter, head or owner free to moderate it (every one of them is in the race or gone) has nobody to ask the questions, so the player's yes to its invitation puts no sitting on the record. The debate waits for the eve of the election and is then held with the player's filed platform as their answers, as a yes did before the sitting existed.
replacement: An outlet's masthead refilled by the jobs engine (refreshPressStaff), or a neutral host the town's league or chamber of commerce names in its records, so every debate has a moderator who asks.
added_by: Words, scenes and the director (debate sitting)

holds_back: A cabinet post the president leaves open (or cannot fill) is marked acting for 210 days (5 U.S.C. 3346(a)(1), sourced); no acting official is named and the department's work is not handed to anyone.

holds_back: Dev mode's custom start as a sitting federal officeholder: the player continues as an eligible adult and takes the seat by writing the offices engine's term and the officials engine's record directly; the record's loyalty and ambition copy the predecessor's.
replacement: A dev-mode custom start owned by OFFICE-LOCAL or OPUS-PLAY that seats any person through the offices and officials engines, with a record built from the person's own traits.

holds_back: The federal officeholder's day keeps its own small tables (the player's stop settings, the week they chose, the day and act records) and finishes the day itself, because OFFICE-LOCAL's one office-day engine is not built yet.
replacement: OFFICE-LOCAL's src/core2/modules/office-day.ts: the federal rows (stops, week, acts) register with it and this module's tables are deleted.

holds_back: A member of Congress's district office takes cases through the cases engine, but the engine brings residents' problems only to the town's own council members and mayor, so a member of Congress receives none.

holds_back: A member learns what the floor takes up today by reading the legislature's calendar keys for scheduled votes; a bill the floor brings up the same day it is filed cannot stop the player and is voted by the character through the legislature's beforeVote hook.

holds_back: The president has no conviction to pardon: the list is empty.

holds_back: What the player prepares for a federal act (the stances a re-election filing runs on, the budget request's line changes, the joint address's answers) is kept in the federal day's own table, beside the engine's.

holds_back: A council or board meets on its own rule for the bills placed before it, but the meetings where members file their own ordinances keep the world-legislating engine's tunable yearly count, so one body has two sets of meeting dates.

holds_back: A state or national party's officers in the standing pool: only the town's local party chair is recorded, so the pool's party officers are the chairs of the state's parties as the town sees them.
