holds_back: A counted resident's engagement with politics, computed with a copy of the views engine's formula (their own key spread around the CES cell average) so the candidacy screen matches the value they get when filled in.
replacement: OPUS-PEOPLE exports an engagement function from views.ts that takes a counted record; candidacy calls it and this copy is removed.

holds_back: Households that move into the counted population are generated in the shape of a household already recorded in the place (ages, sexes, who is family), with new names and temperaments from the world's seed, and arrive with no job, contracts, cash or past on record. Counted babies and newcomers' children get temperaments without their parents' inheritance links.
replacement: Newcomers are generated by the population builder for the place (OPUS-CORE), join the job seekers (OPUS-WORLD jobs) and take a home and purchase contracts (housing, residents flows).

holds_back: A counted baby gets a temperament drawn from the world's seed for its age and place, without its parents' temperaments passed on.
replacement: A counted baby inherits from its counted parents' packed traits through the same family model a full person's child uses.

holds_back: When a couple has no dated partner fact (or it is dated the opening day), the partnership start is estimated: one birth-spacing interval before their first child, else the mother reaching the usual age of a first union.
replacement: Partnerships carry their own recorded start date from the opening's partnership model (OPUS-PEOPLE, opening-partnership).

holds_back: The share of adults with a bachelor's degree (school.college-completion-pct) stays the web's ledger number (base times the links' factors); no engine decides who completes college. The state's higher education line reaches it only there: higher-education-spending-to-college-completion runs in the web on that line, and no engine reads its factor.
replacement: A college engine that gives each graduate an enrollment and completion record by the same standing rule, and a degree on each adult, read back as this measure. That engine, at the moment it decides a graduate's completion, multiplies the graduate's own rate by webReach(api, placeId, "school.college-completion-pct", subject), which is how higher-education-spending-to-college-completion reaches a person; schoolingOn then reads the degree when it prices a hire.

holds_back: A graduate's college enrollment and bachelor's completion are both decided on the day the senior year's graduation is decided, at the national NCES shares (62 percent of completers enroll; 64 percent of first-time full-time starters at four-year schools finish in six years) spread over the income fifths by researched gradients, not year by year in college; the six-year share of four-year starters is applied to every enrolled graduate, two-year enrollees included; every completer holds the bachelor's at normal time (four years), though about a third take longer.
replacement: A completion decided in the spring each enrolled graduate's normal time ends (and later for those who take longer), ranked by the same standing and multiplied by the web's factor for school.college-completion-pct as it then stands, with the NCES shares for the starters at four-year schools and for the two-year enrollees each applied to their own, each in src/core2/data/school/outcomes.json.

holds_back: The share of adults with a bachelor's degree (school.college-completion-pct) stays the outcome web's ledger number (its 2024 base times the links' factors); the degrees the school engine decides for each graduating class are its yearly flow and are not summed into it.
replacement: The measure read from the degrees: the share of a place's adults whose schoolingOn is a bachelor's, with the web's ledger keeping no copy of it (docs/pool/items/web-college-completion-stock-not-accumulated.md).

holds_back: A counted student's attendance in the school standing, and a full student's before they have an attendance record, is the mean attendance share of the same place's full students of that grade, or every school day where the place has none recorded. The standing orders who in an income fifth passes or graduates; it never sets how many do.
replacement: Counted students' attendance from the counted tier's own school days (the same attendance choice full students make, read for the group times its count), so the standing reads one recorded rule in both tiers.

holds_back: The equalized-funding law's link into spending per student is the web's number; no law handler moves the schools budget line, so the school spending measure does not follow the law.
replacement: A law-reach handler that moves the schools line of the budget in force (moveBudget), which the school engine's spending measure then reads. The graduation effect of that spending then runs through school-spending-to-attainment (the schools line above its Census base), so equalized-funding-to-graduation, the reduced form of the same study through the law, is dropped in the same change.

holds_back: The share of public school students who are Hispanic (school.hispanic-enrollment) stays the web's ledger; no engine decides it, so the enforcement link into it (enforcement-to-hispanic-enrollment, which runs in the web on the 287(g) partnership law) moves only that number.
replacement: An enrollment record by ethnicity (from the opening's school enrollment, src/core2/opening-public-schools.ts) that the school engine decides, with a student's ethnicity from the opening's population counts; at the moment it decides whether a student stays enrolled it multiplies the student's own rate by webReach(api, placeId, "school.hispanic-enrollment", subject), which is how enforcement-to-hispanic-enrollment (-0.10 after 24 months, Dee and Murphy 2020) changes who stays enrolled, read back as this measure.

holds_back: Which seniors sign to play at a Division I school is ranked by the school standing plus three personality traits (competitive, persistent, voluntary effort), because no record in the world gives a student's athletic ability, teams or sports. The traits only rank the seniors; the count comes from the NCAA rate and the place's students.
replacement: A student's sports and athletic ability as a record (a body and fitness record that grows with practice, and school teams with rosters), read by the honors in place of the traits, which then only break ties.

holds_back: Every place with students in grades 5 to 8 holds a spelling bee each year and crowns one winner, though not every school or district enrolls in the Scripps program, and a real place has several schools whose champions meet in a district or county bee.
replacement: The district's enrollment in the bee program as a record, a bee in each enrolled school and a district or county bee among their champions, so a place without a bee crowns no one and a place with several schools crowns several.

holds_back: Every place opens owing no school honors: each place's remainder (the fraction of a spelling-bee or Division I signing its students were expected to earn) starts at zero on the day the world opens, though the years before the start would have left each place somewhere between zero and one.
replacement: The school years before the start run the honors (the same rule, each past year's students and rate) so every place opens with the remainder its past leaves it.

holds_back: Every Division I signing of a senior class is decided on one day, the first Wednesday of December (the football early signing period), though the signings fall across the early period, the first Wednesday of February and the other sports' November and April periods.
replacement: One row per signing period in honors.json, each with the share of the year's Division I signings that fall in it, from NCAA signing-period data.

holds_back: Seven researched links into school outcomes do not run, each because its cause is not recorded: class-size-to-scores (no K-3 class size), police-killing-to-graduation (no police killing, and the effect is for students who live near one), daca-to-graduation (no deferred action; a student's immigration status is seeded at both tiers, isUnauthorized in src/core2/citizenship.ts, but children take the adult citizen share), homicide-nearby-to-scores (no homicide below the place, and the effect is for a child tested right after one on their block), lead-to-reading (no blood lead), heat-to-learning (no school-year temperature) and carbon-monoxide-to-absence (no carbon monoxide). school-move-to-scores is no longer one of them: the school engine reads a student's own move (stopgap SG-SCHOOL-switch-window). Family income reaches only math: family-income-to-scores is carried by poverty-to-math-proficiency, and nothing moves reading proficiency by family income.
replacement: Record each cause (class size, blood lead, school-year heat, carbon monoxide, a police killing or homicide with a place below the town, deferred action, with a child's own noncitizen share for student status) or a per-student exposure record, size the link from its study in the engine's units (for a standard-deviation effect on a proficiency share, the normal-density conversion at the base share as school-move-to-scores does), and read it where the engine named above decides, as the school-move read in decideSchoolOutcome does. A reading link from family income needs the poverty-to-math-proficiency per-point size confirmed first.

holds_back: The cause of school-spending-to-attainment is the schools line of the town's city and county budgets above its Census base, standing for the study's change in per-pupil spending. It equals that change only while enrollment stays at the base the line was drawn for: enrollment growth that outruns the line, which lowers spending per student, does not register.
replacement: The school engine's spending per enrolled student as the cause, measured against its first reading, once the schools line follows enrollment (and the equalized-funding law moves it), so students leaving or arriving change spending per student as the study's treatment does.

holds_back: A student's school switch (school-move-to-scores) is a household that moved into the town after the school year began (a counted-moves record, direction in, dated after September 1 and by the testing day), and every such move costs the average the study reports whatever its distance or timing. The cost to classmates who did not move, which the study also finds, is not applied, and a move inside the town, which keeps the town's one district, is not a switch.
replacement: Schools below the town (a district's campuses), so a move between campuses of one district is a switch too and each school's share of new students is a record; then the classmates' turnover cost (0.013 standard deviations for a one standard deviation rise in the share of new students) and the move's distance and timing are read where decideSchoolOutcome decides the grade 8 math test.

holds_back: The Campaigns tab lists the coming ballot's races with who runs and their filed stances, and a candidate's name opens their card; the owner's 'clicking a candidate's rally lets you go there and learn their views' has no rally to go to, so there is no rally link.
replacement: A campaign event record (a rally with its venue, date and speaker) the director stages as a scene the player can travel to from the race's row, where the candidate's views are heard; the row then links to it.

holds_back: The filing counter offers at most four replies; an office that takes more races than that shows the four soonest at the counter, and the rest are reached from the office's own view in Travel and from Campaigns.
replacement: The clerk asks which race in the conversation (the words session's clerk lines, point 32) and the counter opens on the race chosen in Travel or Campaigns, so no list is needed at the counter.

holds_back: A filing made at the counter carries no platform: the rules panel's stance form is gone (owner, Oct 28, point 31) and the filing's platform is empty until the elections engine reads the filer's own views.
replacement: fileCandidacy derives the platform from the filer's own view records on each of the contest's positions when none is handed in; the Campaigns row then reads those stances.

holds_back: Hovering a race at the counter shows a card on the office with what the records know (its district, the election day, who holds the seat); it does not yet say what the office does in words.
replacement: An office-duties bank from the words session (one piece per office kind, graded like every bank) that the hover card reads first, the record's facts after it.

holds_back: With fast-forward on (development only), candidates take no campaign turns and volunteers walk no doors, so a race is decided by the voters' leans, parties, the incumbent's record and the impressions earlier days left.
replacement: A coarse campaign that moves each voter group's standing by the campaign's spending and reach, as counted groups are read, so the aggregate effect of a campaign remains.

holds_back: A bill on the player's desk that the character decides on its own is signed when the character's position plus their traits' lean toward signing is not negative; the legislature engine's own rule for any other executive also weighs how settled the law is.
replacement: The legislature engine exports the executive's own choice on a bill, used for the player's character as for any executive.

holds_back: Dev mode's custom start as a sitting state officeholder ends the seat's serving term and writes the player's term into the offices engine's table directly, keeping the previous holder's party; it is not reached in ordinary play.
replacement: An offices-engine function to seat a chosen person for the rest of a term (OPUS-GOV), with the player's own party from the parties engine, called by dev mode.

holds_back: District office hours decide only the cases already open for the state legislator, and the constituent-cases engine routes residents' problems to council members and the mayor only, so a state legislator's office receives none.
replacement: The constituent-cases engine routes a resident's problem to the state legislator whose district covers them as well as to local officials, by the same choice of whom they know best.

holds_back: Item vetoes now strike or reduce appropriation increases and use exact override fractions and joint totals. Special deadlines, external assent, and some protected or mixed appropriation categories remain incomplete.
replacement: An item veto in the legislature engine: the executive strikes (or reduces, where the data allows) budget lines, each item goes back for its override vote at the data's share, and the budgets engine adopts what stands.

holds_back: The state officeholder's day runs on this file's own small module: tomorrow's entries are scheduled the evening before, and any the player has not done by the morning, a stop included, the character does on its own (a stop that lapses is marked so).
replacement: The office-day engine's calendar, stop and simulate-or-do loop, with the state's entries and acts from this file as its rows.

holds_back: The stress a layoff, an eviction or a missed payment leaves is read by the loan and move decisions for full people only; a counted person's decision reads none, because the wider population stores no stress (a counted worker laid off feels the layoff's appraisal for the day of their claim only).
replacement: Keep a counted person's appraised hardship impulse with the date it landed (a row beside the counted record, written where drives.ts appraises it) and read it, decayed by emotion.ts, in hardshipStress; a person filled in from a group would take it into their affect.

holds_back: Conscientiousness shifts who falls seriously ill and who holds behavior-driven conditions for full people only; a counted group draws its illnesses and deaths from the life-table share without its members' traits.
replacement: Counted illness reads the group's mean of the same factor (exp of the slope times each member's level, from the packed trait columns) when a month's owed illnesses are booked; a person filled in from a group already carries their own.

holds_back: Counted people's trait columns do not move with age or life events while they are counted; they are brought to their age norm in one step when filled in.
replacement: Groups apply the same yearly shift to their columns by age band once the counted store can drop a member's cached lean.

holds_back: Two believing rules: a story or speech one resident passes to another goes through believesClaim (the stranger's pull believeStrangerPull, plus closeness to the teller and how well the claim fits the hearer's view, against the trait lean at its weight), while the player's own claim in a conversation is still read by the director's doubtsClaim (src/director/conversation.ts), the flat truthDefaultPull against the raw trait lean, with no closeness, fit or weight.
replacement: The Words line routes doubtsClaim through believesClaim, passing the player as the teller (pool item words-director-claims-shared-rule); truthDefaultPull is then removed.

holds_back: Filing for unemployment weighs only the benefit's share of the lost pay and the layoff's stress beside temperament. Within a town the share is the same for nearly every worker, so temperament decides who skips far more than the study allows (thirds' odds 6 to 20 against 1.32), and the trait weight stays at the general 1.
replacement: The filing reads the household's cash runway and the place's seekers per opening at researched sizes, then traitWeightJobsBenefitsFileClaim is fitted to Vella, Richiardi and van de Ven 2025.

holds_back: How far a household lives from the middle of town is an estimate: a point spread evenly over a disc the size of the place's land area (2020 Census place-county parts), fixed by the world's seed. There are no home addresses or street map, so two households that are neighbors can be recorded far apart. Only the party meeting's attendance reads it.
replacement: Households placed on the town's real streets or tracts (the housing engine's dwellings), and the meeting hall placed with them; the distance cost then reads the real trip.

holds_back: Couples exist only as the opening drew them: no one partners, marries, separates or divorces during play, so the temperament reads that should decide those (extraversion raises the odds of a first marriage 1.35 per standard deviation and openness lowers them 0.77, Jokela et al. 2011; neuroticism raises divorce r = 0.17, agreeableness lowers it r = -0.18, Roberts et al. 2007) have no decision to read them.
replacement: When partnerships form and end in play, the forming and ending decisions read both partners' traits through leanedYes with weights calibrated from those rows by scripts/traits/trait-calibrate.ts.

holds_back: Nothing is faked; this records that two personality decisions have a real producer that a drawn played year rarely reaches: relationships.fall-out (a grudge against the person who decided a layoff, counted deciders now met when confronted, drives.ts confront) and appointments.weigh (a governor refilling a cabinet post whose holder died or left, executive.ts deskReview). In every drawn place measured (Oct 28), the grudges of laid-off workers aimed at outside-market employers, which have no person behind them, and no department head or cabinet member died or left in the year.
replacement: Outside-market employers name a person (their local manager) once the jobs engine records one; until then the decisions are proven by the generated-world tests src/core2/grudge-counted-decider.traits.test.ts and src/core2/cabinet-vacancy.traits.test.ts, and counted in a played year when a drawn year contains the cause.

holds_back: A charge against, or an exposure of, someone serving in a local office is ranked by the press desk as involving every follower of the outlet, named or counted, the way a law in force is.
replacement: The press desk weighs how much a story matters to the outlet's followers by who it concerns (a public official answers to every constituent) for every item kind, owned by the press area, replacing this one-kind rule.

holds_back: Full couples decide on a child from their own age, children, work, income, room, savings, health and closeness, and none of the outcome web's birth links reach them. Counted women take the web's factor per woman (src/core2/births-counted.ts), so a full woman and a counted woman of the same age, tenure and place differ on the links the full decision does not carry: home prices (owners up, renters down), an enforced abortion ban, and the place's drifting birth level.
replacement: A conditions term in the plan score that reads webReach for the woman's own age and tenure, leaving out the links her own records already carry (unemployment), with a weight calibrated in a played year so full births move by the researched size, as counted births do.

holds_back: Five researched links into crime and justice outcomes move nothing, each because the engine that would decide its outcome has no cause, no size or no producer to read. summer-jobs-to-youth-violence: no engine runs a summer jobs program, so no one is a participant, and the 43 percent fall in violent-crime arrests is the participants' own (J-PAL's summary of Heller 2014); the public-safety engine's arrest share-out by age band (arrest in src/core2/public-safety.ts) would read a participant's record once arrests have offenders. graduation-to-incarceration: the research is a person's own drop in the chance of prison (0.76 points for white men, 3.4 for Black men, Lochner and Moretti) with no base chance to make a factor, and no engine decides a person's offense, so the schooling on a person's record (schoolingOn in src/core2/modules/jobs.ts) has nothing to lower (see SG-CORE-crime-offenders and SG-LAW-justice-named-offender-acts). mandatory-minimums-to-incarceration: the state panel study counts mandatory laws and gives no size for one, the question has no starting row and no engine reads it; the court's decision of each counted case (resolveDue in src/core2/public-safety.ts) and a named defendant's custody months (convict in src/core2/modules/justice.ts) would. mandatory-minimum-cut-to-federal-prisoners runs at -0.008, a 0.8 percent fall, which is the anchor's fall in all U.S. prisoners although the link now points at federal prisoners (by the anchor's own arithmetic, about 13,000 fewer of the federal count, the federal fall is about 6 percent, so the size sits on the old base until it is resized); it moves justice.federal-incarcerated-per-100k only in the web's ledger, since no engine sentences or holds federal prisoners and every case is tried in the state's courts. release-lower-level-to-larceny is sized on crime.property (0.0731, the larceny share of the NCVS property total), which the crime engine reads in typeFactor, but no policy question reclassifies low-level offenses, so its cause is never in force. The counted court reads pretrial-detention-to-conviction (resolveDue in src/core2/public-safety.ts), but a named bribery defendant's verdict (hearing and convict in src/core2/modules/justice.ts) is a margin of evidence against the defense, with no rate this proportion can scale, so the named tier does not read it.
replacement: Record each cause (a summer jobs program's participants, a mandatory-minimum floor in a starting law or bill, a low-level-offense reclassification question); give arrests offenders whose own records (schooling, program) an offending engine reads; size each link from its study in the deciding engine's units (the federal cut on the federal count, about -0.06, not the all-prisoner -0.008) and have the engine named above read it; give federal defendants a court engine; give a named defendant's plea a term for custody before trial.

holds_back: A severe disaster does not lower home values: the link needs the disaster's death toll and the disasters module records only the FEMA declaration and its payments.
replacement: Deaths and damage recorded on each disaster by the disasters module, and the housing sales engine reading the web's home-price factor.

holds_back: A severe disaster (Boustan, Kahn, Rhode and Yanguas 2020: severe by deaths, about 25 or more in a county in a decade) is read from the homes FEMA inspected as damaged in the town per resident, not from deaths. The game's disasters kill no one, and FEMA declarations carry no deaths. The reading is a ramp from 0 at the 90th percentile of the game's own FEMA town rows (0.0526 damaged homes per resident) to 1 at the 95th (0.1157), the cutoffs Roth Tran and Wilson 2023 (FRBSF Working Paper 2020-34, p. 7 and p. 24) draw for damages per capita, ranked here over FEMA's town rows matched to a Census place by name (9,887 rows; 7,997 unmatched or ambiguous rows left out) rather than their SHELDUS county-months. The researched size of the three links that start from it (home values -5.2%, out-migration +5%, non-disaster transfers +2%) applies at a reading of 1 and in proportion below it; the study found no effect from milder disasters, and Roth Tran and Wilson find the average FEMA declaration leaves prices flat and then 1.4% higher. A disaster counts for the ten years after it begins (Boustan's decade). The effect applies from the start, though Roth Tran and Wilson find prices strongly higher one to three years after a very severe disaster and strongly lower only over the longer run. A disaster whose damage FEMA's figures do not show for the town (no row, or no recorded population) reads as no severity, though the damage is unknown. A disaster hits only the player's town (the one place the disasters engine keeps records of); other places read nothing.
replacement: Deaths from a disaster recorded by the health engine's cause-of-death records within the incident's dates (SHELDUS-style county damages per capita if a source of them is added as data), read as disaster.severe; and a disasters engine that records damage to businesses, public buildings and people, so severity is not one town figure.

holds_back: The share of households that are food insecure (household.food-insecurity) is a place number in the outcome web's ledger: its start is the USDA state level and web links move it; no household's food budget or SNAP receipt decides it. Three links into it are carried by engines instead (links.json carriedBy): the SNAP maximum's and SNAP receipt's by the benefit and the household's monthly purchases (snap-maximum-to-food-insecurity, snap-to-food-insecurity), and the grocery exemption's by the sales tax, the price review and the same purchases (grocery-exemption-to-food-insecurity). What a household cannot buy of its everyday plan, kept on its month as unpaid everyday spending, stands for going without food, with no food line of its own.
replacement: A food-insecurity record per household from its income, its food prices and its SNAP benefit, counted by weight in world-metrics and read through engineMeasures.

holds_back: Two housing links move nothing through the web: air-conditioning use does not rise or fall with the electricity price, and the share of income a place's renters pay in rent adds no factor to how many people are homeless. The housing engine's own evictions do follow unpaid rent (a named household's lease by its own pay and cash; counted households by their group's pooled arrears, lowest income first), but no played year yet shows that path rising with burden past 22 and faster past 32 percent.
replacement: A sized link (a published slope per cent of price) read by an engine that decides air-conditioning use; for rent burden, a played year with 10 or more court cases that passes the burden checks in src/core2/housing-calibration.test.ts, after which the link is carried by the housing engine.

holds_back: The town hears of a rise in housing.rent from the outcome web's month record, but no engine yet reads the web's rent factor when it sets a lease, so the rise the story reports is not in any lease or rent payment.
replacement: The housing engine multiplies its lease rent by webFactorFor(housing.rent); then this row and the readBy null in data/news/outcome-news.json are replaced by the reading file.

holds_back: The link from a severe disaster to out-migration (Boustan, Kahn, Rhode and Yanguas 2020) does not run: no record says how many people a disaster killed in a place. The disasters engine holds FEMA declarations (type, begin and declared dates) with no deaths, and the research's effect starts at about 100 deaths.
replacement: A per-place count of deaths from a disaster (the health engine's cause-of-death records within the incident's dates) read as the link's cause disaster.severe.

holds_back: A full person's leaving does not weigh the state income tax in force: only counted households do (counted-moves.ts reads the town state's income-tax law and the other states' 2026 table into an income pull). The web's income-tax links are about zero (Young, Varner, Lurie and Prisinzano 2016), so they add nothing on top, and adding them would count the tax twice for counted households.
replacement: A destination-aware pull for full people that uses the same net-of-tax income comparison as pullBetween in counted-moves.ts.

holds_back: Each outcome the web keeps (crime, schooling, coverage, turnout and the rest) stays at its place's real starting level except where a researched link moves it; nothing else in the world moves it.
replacement: Each outcome moved by the engines that cause it (a crime engine, schools, health coverage, elections), with the web's factor on top, and society-wide shifts from recorded causes rather than a monthly chance.

holds_back: Higher graduation is meant to raise adult pay a decade later, but no engine ties schooling to the pay a graduate is hired at, so graduation reaches no household's income and the poverty measure does not move for it.
replacement: Resolved: the jobs engine prices schooling into every hire (hirePay, schoolingWeekly and schoolingOn in src/core2/modules/jobs.ts reading graduationOf in src/core2/school-outcomes.ts; pool item world-schooling-to-pay), and the poverty count (householdPoverty in src/core2/world-poverty.ts) reads that pay, so graduation-to-poverty is carried by those records (links.json carriedBy), proven by src/core2/jobs-graduation-income.test.ts.

holds_back: Reducing occupational licensing (licensing-reform-to-poverty) is meant to open licensed work and raise pay at the bottom, but no engine lets the law change who may take a licensed job, so the law reaches no household's income and the poverty measure does not move for it.
replacement: The jobs engine reads a licensing law row when seekers match to jobs, so a repeal opens licensed jobs to seekers (pool item world-licensing-reform-jobs).

holds_back: The share of residents receiving SNAP (program.snap-receipt) is a place number in the outcome web's ledger, held at the USDA state level: the SNAP benefit pays households and stops those the work requirement reaches, but no field counts them into the number and no web link moves it.
replacement: A world-metrics field counts the SNAP benefit's recipients by weight and engineMeasures reads it, so the food-insecurity record reads the benefit's own households.

holds_back: The Medicaid expansion's and the work requirement's links to health.uninsured-pct are carried by the law reach's coverage records (links.json carriedBy), which the medical bills read, so the outcome web no longer runs them. A place's health.uninsured-pct therefore moves only with unemployment and marriage equality, and health.uninsured-pct to school.graduation-pct (60-month lag) misses the coverage the expansion gives and the requirement takes away.
replacement: The place's uninsured share for the web's graduation link is read from the coverage records the world keeps (employer plans, Medicare, and the reach's Medicaid coverage records, full and counted), so the expansion and the requirement move it through the same records the bills read.

holds_back: baby-bonus-to-births is not run by the outcome web, so it moves nothing (it waits on program.birth-bonus-dollars, and it has no researched size; its research gives no size the game can apply, so the web does not run it); no person, household or organization record changes.
replacement: Superseded by SG-FAMILY-birth-bonus-not-paid: the links this row named that still do not reach an engine's records now wait on that stopgap instead (src/core2/data/outcome-web/unwired.json); any others reach an engine's records (scripts/outcome-web/effect-matrix.ts). It is off the unwired list.

holds_back: incarceration-to-crime is not run by the outcome web, so it moves nothing (no measure: the web does not keep crime.all and no engine produces it; its research finds no effect (about zero), so an engine would multiply by one); no person, household or organization record changes.
replacement: Resolved: the research finds every link this row named about zero, so there is no effect for an engine to read (scripts/outcome-web/effect-matrix.ts grades it not applicable), and it is off the unwired list.

holds_back: release-lower-level-to-larceny is not run by the outcome web, so it moves nothing (no measure: the web does not keep crime.larceny and no engine produces it; nothing in the core records its cause, law.low-level-offense-reclassified); no person, household or organization record changes.

holds_back: A group's lobbyist who remembers how the player voted (circumstance lobby-remembers) says so, subtle or open by their own temper, and what the player answers is kept as a promise or a strained tie. holds_back: A business with no recorded owner (a public employer, an ownerless landlord) applies for a line whenever its cash is below a few months of payroll; owned businesses' owners decide.

holds_back: A town's police, fire, public works and public health departments and its local government offices are paid by the town's own government (its city or village, else its township), a state office in town by its state and a post office by the nation. The opening's data does not say which unit employs a given department, so the link is assumed.
replacement: Each department's employing government read from the Census of Governments employment file by function, so a county health department, a fire district or a state agency's field office pays its own staff.

holds_back: Savings and withdrawals are reviewed monthly with a three-month wallet reserve; extraordinary payments and estate settlement do not yet request bank withdrawals directly. Dormant claims remain owed, not deleted.

replacement: A residents wage-flow payment hook (OPUS-CORE) that posts the same employer share from the law rows in force. Built Oct 16: the residents engine tells every module each counted payday (onCountedWages) and the employer-taxes module posts the share, per worker times the workers the flow pays.

holds_back: A filled-in record whose job stood for less than one job, at an employer with no other counted job, becomes one full job: that employer gains the difference (under one head).

holds_back: The wider population's renters pay rent from their group's money (the place's residents account, kept per group), and the arrears they run up are held per group (households of one kind in one place), not per household: which of the group's households are behind is read from the group's arrears, the ones with the least income first. holds_back: Eviction steps not yet read from official text in force on the opening day (January 20, 2025): of 56 places, 42 have the notice period read, 42 whether a tenant can cure, 38 the hearing period and 41 the stay (all four in 31, marked high); the other values come from secondary summaries, and missing values take the median of the better-sourced places. replacement: Each place's steps read from the official statute text and cited by section, then M1-laws' landlord-tenant law in force. Oct 23, 2026: 46 steps in 21 places read from the statute text in force on January 20, 2025 (data/research/world/eviction-statute-reads-2026.json, checked against housing.json by scripts/research/housing-check.ts); later laws (Hawaii from February 5, 2026, Texas from January 1, 2026, the District from December 31, 2025) are recorded there as dated laterLaw rows for world-housing-eviction-law-dated-phases. Still open for the 25 places above, which need their codes read through Lexis or the courts' rules (research-housing-statutes-remaining).

holds_back: When a counted household with an open eviction case is filled in, the case follows the household and its lease takes up the arrears the group had run up at notice, from the notice date. Whether the arrears carry over, are cured by the fill-in, or the case closes is the owner's call.
replacement: The owner's ruling on carry, cure or close for a counted household's arrears on fill-in (docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md).

holds_back: A state's foreclosure timeline that was not read from its statute (55 places) is taken from secondary summaries; a place with no published average days to complete (42 places) takes the median of its process (nonjudicial 174, judicial 2007, both 2293 days, computed from the 14 published averages) in place of the national average (ATTOM, 563 days in Q2 2026).
replacement: Each place's foreclosure steps read from its statute text and court rules, with its own average days to complete. Oct 23, 2026: ATTOM's national figure and the 14 state averages were reopened (Q2 2025, Q3 2025 and Q2 2026 releases), Texas's steps were read from statute text (now high) and Minnesota's sale notice corrected to six weeks (data/research/world/foreclosure-reads-2026.json, checked by scripts/research/housing-check.ts against foreclosure.json, read by foreclosureSteps in src/core2/housing-foreclosure.ts). Still open: ATTOM publishes per-state averages only for its five longest and five shortest states each quarter, and the other statutes are unread (research-housing-statutes-remaining).

holds_back: An eviction hearing ends in judgment whenever rent is still owed and notice was given, with no judge's discretion, defenses or counsel.
replacement: The courts port: a judge deciding from the record, the tenant's defenses and any right to counsel in the law in force.

holds_back: A place that no Census county table covers and that is not one of the four island areas (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Marianas, the Virgin Islands, which now start from their own Census 2020 rows) starts from the nation's owner share and household-weighted county medians.
replacement: That place's own tenure, rent and value table; if no such place is reachable, delete the fallback and this row.

holds_back: All of a town's rentals belong to one landlord business with no owner; it serves notice by summed pulls of months owed and months late (calibrated to landlords filing at about two months owed), not by an owner's own patience and cash.
replacement: Rentals owned by the town's own landlords (owners of rental businesses and individual owners), each deciding from their traits, cash and the tenant's history.

holds_back: Every lease that exists when the housing records open has its yearly renewal in one of the twelve months after the first review, the month fixed by the hash of the lease id, evenly across the year. No data says when each opening lease was signed.
replacement: Each opening lease's anniversary drawn from the place's renters by year moved in (ACS B25038), by the same lease-id hash.

holds_back: Each owner's purchase year comes from the national move-in distribution by age rank, the loan is a 30-year fixed with the NAR median down payment and no refinancing, and the nation's mortgage shares by age apply in every county.
replacement: FHFA house price index by state and metro for purchase prices, ACS B25038 and B25027 by county, and refinancing waves from the rate history. Oct 23, 2026: ACS 2020-2024 B25038 and B25027 for every state and county are in data/research/world/acs-2024-owner-mortgage-moved-in-by-county.json (Census Bureau; checked by scripts/research/housing-check.ts against the national shares openingMortgages reads in src/core2/housing-mortgages.ts); purchase prices already follow the state FHFA index (homePriceRatio). Reading the county rows, and refinancing from the rate history historicalMortgageRate already holds, is world-housing-mortgages-county-shares.

holds_back: New houses sell only to full renter households; counted renters and households moving in never buy one, so unsold houses pile up.
replacement: Counted renter households and arrivals buy new houses through the same choice and mortgage, once fill-in and arrivals land.

holds_back: Home prices follow FHFA's state house price index through its latest quarter (2026 Q2), and Puerto Rico's from FHFA's developmental index; after the latest quarter, and where FHFA has no index (Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands), they follow consumer prices (CPI-U, which in the data ends in 2025). The seller in a purchase is outside the town.
replacement: A house price step in the economy (the region's incomes, rates and vacancy), territorial price data, and sellers who are the town's own owners (M1-09; world-home-sales-set-the-town-price, world-home-turnover). Oct 23, 2026: Puerto Rico now reads FHFA's developmental all-transactions index (FHFA, 2026 Q2; data/research/world/fhfa-hpi-pr-2026q2.json, checked by scripts/research/housing-check.ts) through homePriceRatio in src/core2/housing-prices.ts; still open for the four island areas and for prices after the last quarter.

holds_back: A place's shelter beds are its state's year-round beds per 10,000 people (HUD 2025 Housing Inventory Count) times its own people, not the beds its Continuum of Care actually lists in or near it.
replacement: Beds by place from the HIC provider rows (geocode to county and place), with occupancy on the count night. Oct 23, 2026: the 2025 HIC project rows are summed by state and city, with HUD geocodes and count-night occupancy, in data/research/world/hud-hic-2025-beds-by-city.json (HUD, 2025; 2,656 city rows; the state rates shelterBeds reads are checked against it by scripts/research/housing-check.ts). Reading them per place is world-housing-shelter-beds-by-place.

holds_back: American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands, which have no HUD Continuum of Care, use the median shelter beds per 10,000 of the three island areas the HIC counts (Guam, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands), an estimate with a spread of 2.47 to 10.9.
replacement: Each territory government's own shelter count. Oct 23, 2026: none found. American Samoa's Department of Human and Social Services publishes no shelter count, and the CNMI Homeless Coalition's 2018 Saipan count (22 sheltered people, reported by the Saipan Tribune) could not be reopened from the cloud (connection reset, then 503), so the island-area median stays (research-housing-statutes-remaining).

holds_back: Completed rentals now admit unassigned households in either tier once income and cash qualify, and consume an actual vacancy. Existing-stock arrivals and departures still lack unit-level assignment.
replacement: Record opening rental units and route their arrivals and departures through the same assignment and release rules.

holds_back: A job that a saved visitor agreement names as its provider's qualification is never ended by a layoff, a quit, a retirement or a move to another job.
replacement: OPUS-CORE lets a visitor agreement re-resolve its qualification to any current qualified worker at the provider; then this filter goes. Resolved by Claude session on the pool item world-agreements-re-resolve-worker, October 19, 2026: deleted src/core2/pinned-jobs.ts and the jobs engine's filters on it. A saved agreement already follows its product jobs' real life in finance-cash.ts (productJobRelations: an ended job drops out and the supplier's current staff in the product occupations carry it; with none, the agreement ends), so a named job's holder may now be laid off, quit, retire or move.

holds_back: Unemployment insurance is built (a claim after a layoff or closure, the state's law in force, a weekly benefit to the worker) but each benefit is paid from the town's outside account, not from the state's unemployment fund, and nothing collects the employers' contributions into that fund.
replacement: State unemployment insurance under the law in force, paid through postJournal from the state's fund.

holds_back: Every state's unemployment insurance pays half the lost weekly pay up to $611 a week for 26 weeks after one waiting week, with a $2,775 base-period minimum (the states' medians).
replacement: registerUnemploymentTerms with the state's terms from lawInForce once the laws module is on the same branch.

holds_back: Counted workers (the wider population) retire, quit, start looking and stop looking by summed pulls (strongestPulls) rather than the shared chooser; they apply to every opening in their place, and an employed counted worker accepts by acceptScore. Counted closures and layoffs also run through this path.
replacement: Fill-in at the moment a counted person meets an employer (OPUS-CORE's fillInPerson), or an aggregate chooser for counted groups agreed with OPUS-CORE.

holds_back: A counted worker who retires draws their place's opening retirees' average income (Social Security and pensions from outside the town), not a benefit from their own earnings record and claim age.
replacement: The core's Social Security claim for counted retirees, with GOV's benefit rules in force.

holds_back: A layoff names the business itself as who decided it.
replacement: The owner or manager person recorded by M1-08, deciding from their own traits and the books.

holds_back: A job offer's deadline stops the player's clock once as a reminder instead of holding it until the player answers; an unanswered offer lapses as the employer's withdrawal.
replacement: A held offer-deadline stop once the play screen shows jobOffersFor with accept and decline controls (OPUS-PLAY). Done: the play screen answers offers (POST /api/jobs/answer), so the deadline stop is held and settleOffer releases it.

holds_back: The opening's job seekers are the jobless working-age adults whose money covers the fewest days, as many as the nation's unemployment rate implies against the generated jobs; the other jobless adults sit outside the modeled labor market.
replacement: The two-level population's labor-force counts by place, age and job (CPS and LAUS), with full people filled in from them.

holds_back: Every job held at the opening counts its tenure from the game's start, so each opening worker's first yearly raise reads the steepest year of the tenure profile (about 2.6 points over the market's move) instead of the year their real tenure would put them in (about 1.0 point at the BLS median of 3.9 years).
replacement: An opening start date for each job held at the opening, generated from the BLS Employee Tenure tables by age and industry when the world is generated (who exists may be seeded), read by tenureYears for raises and layoffs alike.

holds_back: A worker at an employer with no business books (a town, county or state government, or another public body) gets the yearly move with the place's pay level but no raise for tenure or how they work, so a public employee's pay does not grow within the job as a private worker's does.
replacement: Within-job raises for public workers by the same withinJobRaise rule, held to the room in the government's personnel budget line (the budgets engine) or set by the step schedule a bargaining or pay law records.

holds_back: Quitting and looking around while employed are now decided by the shared chooser for full and counted workers alike, and win only on a large pay gap, so a played year has far fewer quits than JOLTS reports; the old summed-pull churn that matched JOLTS quit rates is gone.
replacement: The leave and look terms (quitScore, jobsLookBaseline, jobsPayGapWeight) calibrated so a played year's quits per worker match JOLTS total private quits by month, measured in drawn places.

holds_back: The share of the BLS weekly-earnings gap between education levels that holds within one role and employer (jobsSchoolingPayShare, 0.4). Positions are already priced for their occupation, which carries part of the schooling premium, so only a share of the raw gap moves a hire's pay.
replacement: A sourced within-occupation schooling premium (for example from a wage regression with occupation and employer controls) replacing the assumed share, with the share read per occupation.

holds_back: No town income-growth observation or local feedback is available before enough comparable paid-income months exist; the national economy continues from its national records.
replacement: Pre-start town paid-income records produced from the opening economy, so year-over-year feedback can be computed from real records immediately. Done Oct 16 (world-stopgap-macro-missing-record): the national step hears the nation's payroll-income growth over the same twelve months as the estimate of the town's growth (townGrowthEstimatePct on each simulated month), and the town's own paid-income growth takes over by a twelfth of the weight for each comparable month it covers (townGrowthOwnWeight). No month omits local feedback.

holds_back: Opening 30-year mortgage rates after April 2019 are the 10-year Treasury plus the 1990-2019 mean FHFA spread, not a published monthly rate.
replacement: A government monthly mortgage-rate series, or monthly HMDA origination dates if CFPB publishes them. Resolved Oct 20, 2026 (tripwire audit): the spread was sourced and the marker retired when "Macro: the mortgage spread is sourced" landed; the row had stayed open.

holds_back: State and local budgets add no impulse to national output beyond their real average, and neither does the federal budget in a world without the budgets engine. Where the budgets engine runs, the federal budget's change from its base is read each month through macroFiscalMultiplier (Oct 14, OPUS-WORLD).
replacement: Resolved Oct 16 (owner ruling, no fiscal multiplier): the macro engine carries no budget impulse or multiplier. A public dollar moves output through who is paid and what they spend, read by the budgets, regional and jobs engines; the research ranges stay as a check on the totals.

holds_back: Until the town has at least macroTownGrowthMinMonths of recorded income with the same months a year earlier (about 15 months into a game), the national step hears a neutral stand-in for the town's income growth: trend growth plus the inflation anchor.
replacement: The town's income history before the start (from the opening's pre-start years), so growth is read from the first month. Deleted the invented neutral growth input and its published observation. Until comparable paid-income records exist, the national model omits local feedback. Actual observed growth still enters the same model; missing pre-start income history remains explicitly registered as SG-WORLD-macro-income-history.

holds_back: Completed rentals match local rent-saving tenants, recovered homeless households, and unassigned households in either tier. Job-location and family-space matching are not modeled.
replacement: Read recorded job locations and dwelling capacity to weigh commute and family-space changes with the same decision rule in both tiers.

holds_back: The bank holds opening mortgages whose original funding is an unmatched opening liability, not named customer deposits. New savings deposits are actual journal transfers and are accounted for separately.
replacement: Generate the mortgage opening with named depositor or warehouse-funding liabilities and retain those funding records in the bank books.

holds_back: The record a screen would read for a business's books (cash, sales, costs, wages, profit, taxes paid and owed, its credit line) is built, but no screen shows it: whether a player sees another business's books is the owner's open decision.
replacement: The owner's ruling on who sees a business's books (its owner, the player as owner, public filings only, or anyone), after which OPUS-PLAY shows this record on the screen that ruling names. docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md: 'Starting or buying a business: 1.0, not early access. An owner sees the books.' and 'a business closing shows its books' as a dev-mode item. The view (business-books-view.ts) is the owner's and the developer's.

holds_back: The player's household is evicted like any other when its rent goes unpaid: notice, filing, hearing, judgment and removal under the place's law.
replacement: The owner's ruling: keep it as is, or give the player's household another path. docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md, 'Homelessness is a factor' (Oct 14): 'A person who does not work and does not pay loses their home like anyone else; the player's household too.' Same notice, filing, hearing and judgment as anyone (docs/packages/homelessness.md).

holds_back: Puerto Rico place 7237336's counted renter households earn about a third of the ACS income, so half of them pay over 72 percent of income in rent on day one; their living-cost arrears then push 17 households into homelessness (76 per 10,000 against HUD's 6.5), and the housing-calibration case is pinned to that count instead of the HUD bound.
replacement: Correct the counted renters' income to the place's sourced ratio (world-counted-renter-income-puerto-rico-third), then remove the pin so the case meets the HUD bound.

holds_back: Each household takes a public broadband offer as the subscribing share of one household, not by its own choice.
replacement: Each household's subscription and its own choice to switch, from its price and service.

holds_back: Property tax is paid a twelfth each month, as through a mortgage escrow, for every owner.
replacement: Bills on the county's due dates from the law in force, with escrow monthly only for owners with a mortgage.

holds_back: Every owner pays the state's average effective property tax rate, to the outside account, with no assessment cap.
replacement: registerPropertyTax with the county's rate, cap and treasury from the law in force.

holds_back: Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Marianas and the Virgin Islands start from their own latest published unemployment rate held flat (src/core2/data/regional/territories.json; American Samoa from the 2020 Census, the Marianas from a 2017 survey), with the nation's pay and price level and no industry mix.
replacement: Each territory's own published labor and price statistics (Guam BLS-funded surveys, USVI Bureau of Economic Research, CNMI and American Samoa statistical offices), or the nearest comparable economy, labeled with its source.

holds_back: A legislative seat whose district has no contested 2024 result on record keeps its real 2026 holder's party in every world: the uncontested seats (safe for their party) and the whole chambers that did not vote in 2024 (Alabama, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, New Jersey and Virginia elect in other years; Nebraska's is nonpartisan; Washington's and the District's results are not in the file). Only seats a world's swing carries across even change hands.
replacement: Each such seat's last contested result (2022 or 2023 returns for the chambers that vote in other years, the district's presidential vote where none), read the same way.

holds_back: Sales in Salem County, New Jersey and in the state's Urban Enterprise Zones are taxed at the full state rate of 6.625 percent; by state law their sellers collect half that, 3.3125 percent.
replacement: A county and zone sales-tax row read from the state statute, so a seller in Salem County or an Urban Enterprise Zone charges its reduced state rate.

holds_back: The town's small-dollar lender pays no costs and draws nothing out: every dollar of interest and fees its borrowers pay stays in its cash and is lent again, so its room to lend grows with each month's interest.
replacement: The lender's costs (storefront rent, wages, charge-offs) and its owner's draw paid out of its cash each month, sized from the sourced industry margin (the operating costs and pre-tax margin of publicly traded payday lenders' annual reports, or the CFPB's and FDIC's studies of storefront lending costs), so its room to lend is its capital plus what it keeps after costs.

holds_back: A town whose drawn yearly small-dollar volume could not fund one $100 loan gets no lender record, so its households short of money have no high-cost lender at all, and the consumer-loan cap has nothing to bind there.
replacement: Borrowers in a town without a storefront reach the nearest place's lender (a coarse-tier lender for the county or the nearest place with one), quoted under the law in force where the lender operates.

holds_back: One small-dollar lender record stands for every high-cost lender in a town (storefront payday, installment, vehicle title and online), at the state's one sourced rate, payday or installment by state. It checks every applicant for its own earlier charge-offs, where the CFPB finds only some lenders check a specialty credit reporting firm for earlier payday defaults (white paper, April 2013, page 9). A lender never opens or closes in play: a state that repeals its cap or bans the product gains or loses none. The outcome web's factor on high-cost lenders (the count of storefronts the research moves) stands in for lenders closing by shrinking what the one lender lends a household, not by turning households away, and the cap's ceiling lowers the payment a household weighs, so under the cap a household short of money is as likely or likelier to borrow, where the research finds use falls as lenders leave.
replacement: One lender record per storefront, from the place's share of the state's Census consumer-lending establishments (data/research/outcome-web/place-outcome-bases-2024.json, finance.high-cost-loans), each with a product (payday, installment, title) and its own rate, opening and closing as the law in force and the web's count move.

holds_back: A household with any open loan, the bank's or the storefront's, asks neither the bank nor the small-dollar lender: the lender copies the bank's one-open-loan rule, so a payday borrower never holds two payday loans at once or a payday loan beside a bank loan.
replacement: Each state's limit on concurrent small-dollar loans as a row in src/core2/data/credit/small-dollar.json (from the state's statute, e.g. NCSL's payday lending statutes table), read where the lender quotes, with the bank's own rule kept for the bank.

holds_back: A relative living out of town (a husk) is never an aide candidate, because the records hold no work for them, and an unknown job is not an empty one.
replacement: Work for out-of-town relatives from their place's coarse population (jobs by age and place), after which those within commuting reach and out of work apply like anyone.

holds_back: An official whose office sits outside the town (a state or federal office, at its seat of government) draws one applicant living where the office sits, generated from the world's seed and the office (name, age in the business-worker range, traits), and records them as a person only when hired.
replacement: The seat's coarse population (people by age and work, as the town's counted population is kept), from which the official's applicants come by the same reach and working-age reads.

holds_back: A counted employer short of cash on payday records a wage shortfall and never draws its approved credit line, though the line has room.
replacement: A finance-engine draw for a residents wage flow (journal-balanced, up to the line's room), called from residents settle() before the shortfall is recorded.

holds_back: When a filled-in household's weight spreads over its group, the households that take it stand for more people while their jobs keep the heads they stood for, so the added people stand for no job and never become counted job seekers.
replacement: The jobs engine reads each counted record's working-age people beyond its jobs' heads as counted seekers, with the same chooser as everyone else (pool item world-weight-release-jobless-seek-work).

holds_back: A local flat income tax on a row whose base is wages or AGI is taken on the paycheck's gross pay (no pre-tax contributions or personal exemptions are modeled); a row whose base is taxable income is taken after the state (else federal) standard deduction only.
replacement: Personal exemptions and adjustments read from the law rows and the worker's own records.

holds_back: A worker who lives outside the town pays no county or city income tax to the town's jurisdictions for working there (the rows' nonresident rate is not applied); local tax is withheld only by the law at the worker's residence.
replacement: Resolve the workplace's local chain per paycheck and apply each row's nonresident rate to residents of other jurisdictions.

holds_back: Income tax a worker owes a government with no treasury in the world (another state, or a county or city the world does not model) is not withheld, so the worker's pay is not reduced by it and no money moves.
replacement: Each such government gets a treasury (or an obligation-backed outside flow) and the withheld tax is paid to it.

holds_back: Payroll withholding for a worker who lives outside the town reads the law of the worker's residence from the starting-law rows (the town's recorded rows where a jurisdiction is shared with the town), so a law enacted in play in a jurisdiction the town does not share is not read; a residence the place lookup cannot resolve gets federal and payroll tax only.
replacement: Each place's law chain recorded in the laws module, enacted acts included, read for every worker's residence.
